stories.headline: Renowned Telugu actor G.V. Narayana Rao dies
stories.deck: Rao, a contemporary of superstars Chiranjeevi and Rajnikanth, acted in about 100 films and several TV serials
stories.bodyText:
Renowned Telugu actor G. V. Narayana Rao died here following a heart attack, actress Karate Kalyani said on Thursday (August 27, 2026).
Rao was 73.
Ms. Kalyani stated in a social media post that Rao died on Wednesday (August 26, 2026) night.
The funeral would be held on August 28 at Vaikunta Mahaprasthanam crematorium in the city, she said.
Rao made his debut in 1976 with 'Antuleni Kadha' directed by veteran K. Balachandar.
Rao, a contemporary of superstars Chiranjeevi and Rajnikanth, acted in about 100 films and several TV serials.
Some of his successful films include 'Chilakamma Cheppindi', 'Muthyala Pallaki', Chiranjeevi's 'Gang Leader' and 'Hitler'.
Rao acted in popular serials such as 'Pasupu Kumkuma' and 'Sundarakanda'.

stories.headline: Nepal flash floods: Software engineer from A.P.’s Kuppam ‘missing’, family appeals for assistance
stories.deck: V.S. Balasubrahmanyam had travelled to Nepal on August 13 with a batch of Kailash Manasarovar Yatra pilgrims
stories.bodyText:
A software engineer from Andhra Pradesh’s Kuppam is reportedly missing after the devastating flash floods in Nepal, prompting his family to reach out to the police and the State government for assistance.
According to family members, V.S. Balasubrahmanyam, who is settled in Hyderabad, had travelled to Nepal on August 13 with a batch of the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra pilgrims. “His mobile phone has remained switched off since Tuesday, and the family has not received any information about his whereabouts,” Srikanth, the software engineer’s elder brother, told the Kuppam Police.
Mr. Srikanth also appealed to Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu for assistance in tracing Mr. Balasubramanyam.
The Andhra Pradesh government has launched efforts to identify and evacuate state residents stranded in Nepal. A control room has been set up at A.P. Bhavan in Delhi to coordinate with the Centre and monitor the situation, Deputy SP (Kuppam) Parthasarathy said.
Meanwhile, five residents of Andhra Pradesh are currently untraced. Four pilgrims from Adoni in Kurnool district who travelled to Mana Sarovar have been reported safe.

stories.headline: Norway's King Harald dies aged 89 after more than three decades on throne
stories.bodyText:
Norway's King Harald, the country's ceremonial head of state for more than three decades, died aged 89 on Friday after a period of ill health, the royal palace said. Harald, Europe's oldest living monarch, died peacefully at Oslo University Hospital at 6.35am local time, or 4.35am GMT, where he had been receiving treatment for a bacterial infection in his blood.
"King Harald passed away peacefully at Oslo University Hospital on Friday 28 August, 0635 (local time, 0435 GMT)," the royal palace said on its website.
King Harald's health had weakened in recent years
The king had been admitted to hospital on August 17 after developing the infection. His death comes after a series of health problems in recent years that had increasingly limited his public duties.
Harald was hospitalised in 2024 while on holiday in Malaysia after suffering an infection. He received a temporary pacemaker during treatment there before being flown back to Norway by the Norwegian armed forces. He was later fitted with a permanent pacemaker.

stories.headline: Second flood 'imminent'? Nepal halts rescue ops as China border lake begins overflowing
stories.bodyText:
A lake formed by a landslide on the Nepal-China border began overflowing on Friday, triggering a fresh flood alert and forcing Nepal to temporarily suspend rescue operations in areas devastated by a flash flood two days ago.
Nepal and China have both warned of fresh flooding after Wednesday's catastrophic flash flood killed at least 469 people in Nepal and left nearly 1,000 missing. The disaster was triggered after a glacier collapse in the Himalayas sent huge amounts of ice, rock and water downstream, devastating settlements, bridges and hydropower projects.
Chinese authorities said on Friday that the newly formed lake had grown to more than 2.5 million cubic metres of water, up from an estimated 1.5-2 million cubic metres recorded a day earlier. The rising water has already forced Chinese rescue personnel and vehicles to withdraw to a safer area amid fears of a breach and further landslides and avalanches.
Why is a second flood feared?
Experts are particularly concerned because debris from Wednesday's disaster may have created another temporary blockage in Nepal's Trishuli river. The International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) is assessing whether the debris has formed a landslide dam, which could trap large amounts of water upstream before suddenly releasing it.
“With a blockage still lodged upstream on the Nepal-China border, authorities warn a second flood is imminent,” Qianggong Zhang, head of climate and environmental risks at ICIMOD, told The Independent, which reported that evacuation orders had been issued for Jilong Port because of the risk of another wave of flooding.
The danger is not limited to the lake itself. A sudden breach could send a powerful surge downstream through an already devastated landscape, while the unstable terrain could trigger further landslides, mountain collapses and avalanches.
China's Ministry of Water Resources has warned that another 3 million cubic metres of water could flow into the already dammed lake over the next three days — roughly equivalent to 1,200 Olympic-sized swimming pools. Chinese state media said peak flow was expected around September 1, while rainfall forecast over the coming week could further increase the threat.
“The volume of water is continuing to increase, and so is the risk,” Zhu Jinfeng, a researcher with the ministry's hydrology department, told CCTV.
Chinese authorities have deployed an eight-member engineering team to conduct aerial surveys and 3D modelling of the lake. Engineer Chen Hanxiao said access to the site was difficult because the glacier collapse had left isolated and steep cliffs around the shoreline.
Nepal races to rescue survivors as threat grows
The warnings come as Nepal's rescue operation enters its third day. Nepal Police said 469 people had died across eight districts, while 977 people, including security personnel and foreign tourists, remained missing. A further 1,545 people have been rescued.
More than 7,400 security personnel have been deployed, with helicopters being used to evacuate people from isolated areas and ground teams searching riverbanks and downstream settlements. The Nepal Army has also sent a team to inspect the Bhotekoshi River amid concerns about further flooding.
The disaster has already left entire communities buried under mud and debris. At the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project, rescuers were searching for people believed to be trapped inside a tunnel, although mud had covered its entry and exit points.

briefs.headline: Nepal flash floods LIVE: Fresh flood risk warning issued as water level rises at same disaster site; death toll at 469
briefs.deck: Search and rescue operations halted; Nepal Police also issued an alert after receiving information that a water dam on the Tibetan side had burst again
briefs.bodyText:
The death toll from the massive flash floods that occurred earlier this week in Nepal has reached 469, Nepal police said on Friday (August 28, 2026), issuing a fresh flood warning after the water level increased at the same flash flood site. Nepal Police also issued an alert after receiving information that a water dam on the Tibetan side had burst again.
Chinese state broadcaster CCTV also warned that a dammed lake upstream of the Gyirong border port had begun to overflow.
WATCH | Why did the flash floods happen in Nepal?
Meanwhile, Nepal’s Foreign Ministry said it does not need help from other countries to conduct search and rescue operations. “The offer for help is natural. Our security agencies are doing the search and rescue operation. For now we don’t require such help,” Spokesperson Lok Bahadur Chhetri said. The Red Cross launched an emergency appeal for $31 million, while the Switzerland-based International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) launched the appeal for 25 million Swiss francs.
Also Read | Danger from above: On the Nepal flood
Earth scientists reviewed satellite imagery for clues to the cause and assessed the devastation. Geomorphologists Kristen Cook and Dan Shugar said they could see in satellite images that the bedrock underneath the glacier had collapsed, taking the massive chunk of ice down with it and sending boulders and ice into the valley.

briefs.headline: Kamal Haasan calls for abolition of NEET, backs entrance exam reforms
briefs.deck: Kamal Haasan urged the Centre to clear Tamil Nadu’s NEET Exemption Bill, which is awaiting Presidential assent, and said the focus should be on ending what he described as an unfair system rather than reforming it
briefs.bodyText:
Actor and Makkal Needhi Maiam (MNM) president Kamal Haasan called for the abolition of NEET, arguing that the examination system creates a mismatch between school education and college entrance tests.
In a post on X, Mr. Haasan cited the Union government’s Vineet Joshi Committee, which he said had acknowledged the disconnect between what students are taught in school and what they are tested on for college admissions.
He urged the Centre to clear Tamil Nadu’s NEET Exemption Bill, which is awaiting Presidential assent, and said the focus should be on ending what he described as an unfair system rather than reforming it. For other entrance examinations, Haasan backed the committee’s recommendations, including giving greater weightage to Class 12 marks, allowing multiple attempts during the year and limiting coaching to two to three hours a day.

briefs.headline: Jharkhand CID arrests two more persons in exam 'irregularity' case

The Jharkhand CID has arrested two more accused in connection with alleged irregularities in the JSSC-CGL examination, an official statement said.

briefs.headline: Two teachers suspended in Yadgir for participating in RSS events
briefs.deck: ​According to the suspension order, these two teachers participated in RSS Pathsanchalan events organised in Talikote (Vijayapura district) and Hunsagi (Yadgir district) on October 10 and 12, 2025
briefs.bodyText:
The Education Department has taken strict disciplinary action against two government schoolteachers in Yadgir district for participating in a Pathsanchalan (route march) organized by the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS).
The suspension orders were issued on August 20 by Deputy Director of the School Education Department (DDPI) Channabasappa Mudhol.
The names of the suspended teachers were given as Gururaj Joshi, working at the Government Girls High School in Hunsagi, and Annasaheb Deshmukh, working at the Government Primary School in Kuppi village, located in Shorapur taluk.
According to the suspension order, these two teachers participated in RSS Pathsanchalan events organised in Talikote (Vijayapura district) and Hunsagi (Yadgir district) on October 10 and 12, 2025.
A departmental order explicitly noted that their participation in the organization’s events constitutes a clear breach of Rules 3(1)(2)(3), 5 and 7 under the Karnataka Civil Services (Conduct) Rules 2021. The order cited dereliction of duty as the reason for the suspension.
Under the terms of the suspension, both teachers are required to strictly adhere to government service protocols throughout the suspension period.
The administrative action follows a complaint lodged by district president of the Ambedkar Swabhimani Sene, Yadgir, Jummanna Gudimani to the then Minister for Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Priyank Kharge and the State government seeking disciplinary action against the teachers.

briefs.headline: The bygone movie theatres of Chennai: a compilation
briefs.deck: This is a collection of stories by The Hindu on the popular single screens and theatre complexes that are etched in the memories of cinephiles of Chennai city even years after they ceased existing.
briefs.bodyText:
As Chennai city celebrates the 387th anniversary of its founding this year (as Madras Day), The Hindu looks back at the city’s iconic cinema halls that reveal a rich tapestry of cultural history and changing urban landscapes. Long before the era of modern multiplexes and malls, single screens and theatre complexes served as the vibrant heartbeat of movie buffs in the city.
From the legendary Udhayam Theatre Complex in Ashok Nagar—hailed as the ultimate “collection king” and a premier first-day-first-show destination—to the architectural marvels of Safire Theatre on Mount Road that once defined the city’s cosmopolitan pulse, these spaces shaped generations of memories.
Though many of these historic landmarks including the Pilot Theatre at Royapettah and National Theatre at Virugambakkam have since given way to commercial/residential real estate and high-rises, revisiting their legacy offers a nostalgic and poignant glimpse into the golden age of moviegoing in Madras, reminding residents of the enduring cultural roots underlying Chennai’s rapid metropolitan transformation.
Their stories also mirror the city’s own transformation: neighbourhoods grew, audiences changed, technology altered the business of exhibition, and old cinema spaces gradually disappeared or were repurposed.

briefs.headline: Glacier break or earthquake? What triggered the Nepal floods? | Explained
briefs.deck: The evidence now points to a large collapse of ice and rock high in the Himalayas near Langtang Lirung, rather than heavy rainfall.
briefs.bodyText:
The story so far: A devastating flash flood in the Bhote Koshi–Trishuli river system has killed at least 389 people in Nepal and three in Tibet, while more than 1,400 people are reported missing. Hundreds of people have been displaced in affected districts including Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha and Chitwan No deaths have been reported in India so far, but 288 Indian nationals in Nepal remain uncontactable, with 84 Indians rescued and authorities in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh monitoring downstream flood risks. Roads, bridges, homes and hydropower infrastructure have been destroyed, and search, rescue and relief operations are under way.
What caused the flood?
The evidence now points to a large collapse of ice and rock high in the Himalayas near Langtang Lirung, rather than heavy rainfall. A mass of glacier ice, rock and debris appears to have detached at about 5,200 metres and fallen roughly 1,200 metres into the Lhende Khola system by momentum, gathering more rock, sediment, ice and water and morphing into a fast-moving debris flow. The rubble temporarily blocked the river and the resulting surge then travelled downstream through the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli systems, affecting communities nearly 100 km away.
Why was an earthquake initially suspected?
Seismological instruments detected a strong ground signal at about 8.37 a.m. on August 26. It was initially interpreted as an earthquake of roughly magnitude 4.4. Because the flood followed almost immediately, the natural explanation was that an earthquake had shaken loose a landslide or glacier, which then blocked the river.
Editorial | Danger from above: On the Nepal flood
That interpretation has since changed. Analysis by the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) found that the seismic signal originated in a glaciated mountain cliff and was generated by the collapse itself. A second seismic event, about three hours later, produced energy equivalent to a magnitude-4.2 earthquake. A preliminary assessment by the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) of ISRO provides important evidence about the origin of the Nepal floods. NRSC compared a pre-event Sentinel-2 image from August 24 with a post-event Resourcesat-2A image acquired on August 26, as well as with an earlier Resourcesat-2A image from April. It provides independent visual evidence of a major physical change at the suspected source area, complementing the seismic evidence that places the ground-vibration source in a glaciated mountain cliff on the north side of Langtang Lirung. However the precise mechanics of the collapse are still being reconstructed.
So how can a non-earthquake produce a “4.2”?
A seismometer does not identify an earthquake by itself. It records ground vibrations. Earthquakes are the most familiar source, but large landslides, volcanic eruptions, explosions and glacier collapses can also shake the ground.
The magnitude figure therefore describes the size of the seismic energy recorded, not necessarily the cause. In this case, the collapsing mass was so large and moved so rapidly that it generated seismic waves comparable to those produced by an earthquake. USGS estimates that the initial collapse released energy equivalent to about a magnitude-5.2 earthquake.
What is an ice-rock avalanche?
It is essentially a rapidly moving mixture of ice and rock released from a steep mountain slope and in the process of descent incorporating snow, water, soil, boulders and other material. The result can behave less like a conventional landslide and more like a highly destructive, mobile debris flow. In Nepal, the material entered a river, temporarily dammed it and then generated an enormous downstream flood.
Was this like the South Lhonak GLOF in October ‘23?
In the 2023 South Lhonak disaster in Sikkim, a glacial lake burst, releasing stored water and producing a flood downstream, draining about 105 hectares of the lake.. A GLOF, or glacial lake outburst flood, requires a lake and the sudden failure of its natural dam whereas the Nepal event appears instead to have begun with the collapse of ice and rock. The two hazards can nevertheless overlap wherein an ice or rock avalanche can fall into a glacial lake, generate a wave and cause the lake to breach.
Why can’t glacier collapses be predicted?
Because scientists can often identify hazardous conditions without knowing when failure will occur. This is like predicting which specific straw will break the proverbial camel’s back. A steep glacier may remain apparently stable for years and then fail suddenly. Temperature, meltwater, cracks, bedrock instability, permafrost and freeze-thaw processes can all influence stability, but there is no reliable equivalent of an earthquake forecast that says a particular glacier will collapse at a particular time.
Can satellites track glaciers?
Yes. Satellites can repeatedly measure glacier area, movement, elevation, snow cover and the growth or shrinkage of glacial lakes. Radar satellites can also observe through clouds, while optical imagery provides detailed before-and-after pictures. ISRO, for example, uses satellite data to monitor glaciers, glacial lakes and landslide-dammed water bodies. For all this, their important limitation is that they mostly observe change rather than predict sudden failure. Satellite revisit times, cloud cover, resolution and the difficulty of obtaining measurements in inaccessible high-altitude terrain constrain monitoring.

briefs.headline: Kolkata Police register case against TMC’s Abhishek, Derek O’Brien for scuffle over removal of a party hoarding
briefs.deck: Three FIRs have been lodged against the TMC leaders for allegedly assaulting police personnel, obstructing them to discharge their duty, and also attempting to outrage the modesty of a lady police personnel.
briefs.bodyText:
The Kolkata Police have registered FIRs against the Trinamool Congress general secretary Abhishek Banerjee and Rajya Sabha MP Derek O’Brien on Friday (August 28, 2026) for allegedly assaulting police and obstructing them from discharging their duty when they went to remove an electric signboard of the party at a building in Kolkata’s Camac Street area. Three FIRs have been registered in connection with the scuffle.
“The removal was being done as per the direction of Kolkata Municipal Corporation. At least 13 people have so far been arrested in the case. All three FIRs by the police, and KMC officials have been reported at the Shakespeare Police Station,” Additional Commissioner of Police (Crime), Kunal Aggarwal said on Friday (August 28).
Mr. Agarwal said that accused including Derek O’Brien, Abhishek Banerjee, Humayun Kabir, Baisanor Chattopadhyay and others. “These leaders along with their supporters, formed an unlawful assembly, obstructed and restrained the police personnel and KMC officials from entering the common area and discharging their lawful duties, and used criminal force and assault against police personnel, including lady police personnel, and KMC officials,” the police said.
A scuffle between Trinamool Congress leader and KMC officials and the police personnel erupted on Thursday (August 27) night when personnel of Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC), forcibly removed a billboard from a building in Kolkata’s Camac Street area, where a party office is located.
A billboard reading ‘All India Trinamool Congress’ was put on the top of a building located at 9 Camac Street, and a large part of the premises serves as the office of Mr. Banerjee. The police and the KMC officials argued that several offices are located in the building and a billboard of a political party cannot be put on it.
A large number of policemen, along with some officials of KMC, arrived at the address and tried to enter the building to remove the billboard at about 3.30 p.m. in the afternoon. Mr. Banerjee and other Trinamool leaders tried to stop the police and asked if they had necessary orders to enter the building.
For the next one and half hours, heated exchange broke out between the Trinamool Congress leaders and police and municipal officials. Trinamool Congress supporters raised slogans but the police eventually forced their way inside and removed the banner. Trinamool Congress Rajya Sabha MP Derek O’ Brien fell on the stairs as police and other officials reached the roof to remove the hoarding. Videos shared by the Trinamool Congress on social media showed pushing and shoving between party supporters and the police personnel.
“What bill board will I put outside my office, will this be decided by the BJP. There are 400 posters of the BJP on this road. Will the police and KMC remove any of them,” Mr. Banerjee asked.
In the FIR, police have alleged that the billboard was hanging dangerously and therefore the KMC directed to remove it immediately from the space. While assisting the KMC officials, some unknown persons obstructed the police personnel on the staircase and snatched the government issued walkie-talkie wireless from a constable. When he tried to apprehend one of them, the persons allegedly assaulted the police personnel, causing injuries.
It is further alleged that a lady police personnel was attacked with intent to outrage her modesty, and that the accused persons threatened the public servants with false criminal cases and consequences to their service, thereby intimidating and deterring them from performing their lawful duties.
The first FIR by the deputy manager of the KMC (Advertisement), Sandeep Kumar Bose, was lodged under sections 191(2), 191(3), 190, 121(1), 351(2), 303(2), 3(5) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The second FIR by the injured constable of Park Street Police Station, Sujit Kumar Mandal was lodged under sections 304(2) and 121(1) of BNS. Meanwhile, the third FIR was lodged based on a written requisition of KMC. It includes sections 191(2), 191(3), 190, 121(1), 74, 3(5), 351(2) of BNS.

briefs.headline: Chennai’s Anand Theatre was the ‘OG’ for the city’s old film-buffs
briefs.deck: The Anand theatre in Mount Road was the one to stake its claim as “the first 70mm theatre of South India”
briefs.bodyText:
In the year of 1964, the Madras State saw two 70mm theatres in fairly close succession, but the one to stake its claim as “the first 70mm theatre of South India” was Anand theatre. It was built on Mount Road by G. Umapathy who ran Uma Printers. On August 22, 1964, this modern theatre was inaugurated by former Chief Minister K. Kamaraj, the president of the Congress party at the time.
About two days later, its inaugural film, the historical drama El Cid premiered and drew many notable personalities, including M. Bhaktavatsalam, then Chief Minister of the Madras State. For many of the film buffs of Chennai, Anand was more of a ritual where they went to watch English films.
A dermatologist and resident of Chennai, Arjun Mathuranayagam, remembers being taken there by his parents, who were “the biggest film buffs”, particularly through the 60s, 70s, and 80s. “Anand holds the record for the longest unbroken run by any English movie in Madras History — Bruce Lee’s Enter the Dragon — at 54 weeks,” says Dr. Mathuranayagam. He also clearly remembers the theatre as much as the films he watched there. “The screen was massive and deeply curved so as to completely cover a 70mm Super Panavision projection in all its glory,” he adds, pointing out how nothing comes quite close to Anand today.
Subsequently, Little Anand theatre was built in the same complex, where Tamil films such as Vennira Aadai had a long and successful run. Retired Chennai resident Rajamani Rajkumar has fond memories of the theatre. He says the proximity of Anand and Little Anand allowed audiences at Anand to sometimes faintly hear the dialogues from the film playing next door. “I grew up in Mylapore, and used to reach Anand in less than 15 minutes in the 70s with no traffic. I remember watching so many English films, which were all brought to India two years after their release abroad,” says Mr. Rajkumar.
Even as a child, Mr. Rajkumar remembers watching films such as Arabesque, a spy comedy thriller at Anand. It was the 2001: Space Odyssey that stayed with him. “After watching the film, my father took me to meet theatre owner G. Umapathy, and I had some cool drinks at his office,” reminisces Mr. Rajkumar. “There were snacks sold at the theatre, but some also went to McRennett nearby before heading for the film. During the 60s and 70s, people watched the films at Anand with so much discipline,” he adds.
The crowd eventually thinned by the 1990s, and in the early 2000s, Anand felt the tides turning. A Behindwoods report in 2006 quoted a spokesperson from Anand theatre as saying that movie piracy had significantly affected the theatre’s profits and all screenings were stopped permanently. That is how the theatre was eventually removed from Mound Road. But landmarks do not disappear that easily. The Anand theatre may no longer stand there physically, but its name still lives on at the Anand theatre bus stop, and in little fragments in the minds of the city’s old film buffs.
Published - August 27, 2026 07:23 pm IST

stories.headline: Bengaluru Cyber Crime cop among 4 killed as bus plunges from bridge in MP
stories.deck: A passenger bus traveling from Bengaluru to Indore overturned on the Bhopal bypass. The accident resulted in four fatalities and eleven injuries among the passengers. Among the deceased was a Bengaluru police inspector on duty searching for an accused. Several passengers were thrown from the bus, falling about thirty feet below. Injured individuals were transported to nearby hospitals for medical…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Four people, including a Bengaluru police inspector, were killed and 11 others injured after a passenger bus overturned and crashed into a 30-foot-high bridge on the Bhopal bypass in Biaora city of Madhya Pradesh's Rajgarh district on Friday morning.
The bus was travelling from Bengaluru to Indore when the accident occurred. Among those killed was Inspector Ravi KV, who was part of a Bengaluru Cyber Crime team travelling to Madhya Pradesh in search of an accused, Additional SP KL Banjare said.
The other three deceased were identified as bus driver Vikas Shukla, Belal Ali, son of Kalimullah Mian, and Jyotiraditya Singh God, son of Vikram Singh Gaud of Bijwad.
Four fall from bus
According to police, the bus lost control and collided with the bridge on the Bhopal bypass. The impact threw around four passengers from the bus, causing them to fall onto the service road about 30 feet below.
The injured were taken to nearby hospitals. Four of them are reported to be in critical condition.
Three members of the Bengaluru Cyber Crime team were injured in the accident. They were identified as Sub-Inspector Ramesh Naik, ASI Srinivas and technical staff member Vishwanath. Srinivas was referred to another hospital in critical condition.
Family travelling to Ujjain
A family from Uttar Pradesh's Jaunpur was among those travelling on the bus. Amit Kumar Pratap said he was travelling with his wife Meenu Singh, 13-year-old son Rakshit Singh and father-in-law Surendra Pratap Singh to Ujjain for Mahakaleshwar temple darshan.
Several other passengers from Uttar Pradesh were also injured in the accident.
The injured have been identified as Amit Kumar Pratap, Vinod Kumar Singh, Meenu Singh, Rakshit Singh, Surendra Pratap Singh, Ravi Sharma, eight-year-old Parth Sharma, Suman Sharma, Srinivas, Keshav, Ramesh Naik, Sonu and Vishwanath.
Surendra Pratap Singh, Suman Sharma and Srinivas were referred to hospitals in Bhopal for further treatment.

stories.headline: Arms supplier shot in leg after attacking cop during midnight operation in Bengaluru
stories.deck: Following a dramatic midnight raid, authorities apprehended Zeeshan, a suspected maker of illegal arms. In a desperate attempt to escape, he attacked a police constable and unleashed chilli powder at the officers. A police sub-inspector then fired, wounding Zeeshan in the leg. Both he and the constable received prompt medical attention. This operation is linked to an ongoing murder investigation…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: A midnight operation to track down a suspected illegal arms maker took a dramatic turn when the accused attacked a police constable with a weapon and later hurled chilli powder at the police team in Somasundarapalya.
Acting on credible information, Bandepalya police inspector Manjunath RV deputed police sub-inspector Sachin Gowda and a team to trace Zeeshan, 34, a resident of Subashnagar, Electronics City, who was suspected to be involved in arms-making and supplying activities.
Police also suspect him to be an associate of Adil Akmal, who was arrested in connection with the murder of Suhail under Madivala police jurisdiction on Aug 22 over enmity.
The police team, comprising Sachin and constable Sandeep Kamble, located Zeeshan near Somasundarapalya Lake around 12.50 am on Thursday midnight. However, when he noticed the police, Zeeshan allegedly took out a weapon and attacked Kamble, causing injuries to his left hand.
In an attempt to protect the injured constable and bring the situation under control, Sachin fired a warning shot into the air with his service pistol. 
Despite this, Zeeshan continued attacking the police and threw chilli powder at them.
With the situation escalating, Sachin fired another round, hitting Zeeshan in his right leg. Zeeshan collapsed due to the injuries.
Both Zeeshan and constable Kamble were immediately rushed to Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopedics Centre, Jayanagar, for treatment. According to police, both are out of danger.
A scene-of-crime officer (SOCO) team inspected the spot, while the area was secured for further investigation. Senior police officials also visited the spot, hospital and police station following the incident.
A case has been registered at Bandepalya police station under Sections 109 (attempt to murder), 132 (assault or criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging his duty), and 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace) of the BNS and under the Arms Act.
Suhail, 37, a medical store owner, was hacked to death by a gang with lethal weapons while he was riding on his Harley-Davidson bike along with his friend, heading from Madiwala towards Koramangala, around 9.45 pm.
Madiwala police had arrested five persons in the case. The arrested allegedly confessed that the weapons were supplied to them by Zeeshan.

stories.headline: Nepal flash floods: 8 from Bengaluru stranded, rescue efforts on, says Deputy CM G. Parameshwara
stories.deck: Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar speaks to survivor from State, assures support
stories.bodyText:
Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara on Thursday (August 27, 2026) said eight people from Bengaluru were stranded in Nepal following the flash floods, and steps are being taken to rescue them.
“We have no information about any deaths. A helpline has already been opened. People can contact 1070 or 080-22253707, and necessary action will be taken. If any of your family members or acquaintances are unreachable, please inform us immediately,” the Deputy Chief Minister said during a press conference here.
He said senior officials will be sent to Kathmandu, and further action will be taken based on the information received.
“We have shared all the information officially available so far. The Resident Commissioner in Delhi has also been contacted and instructed to take immediate action,” he said.
Home Minister Priyank Kharge has separately urged Indian citizens affected by the floods to make immediate use of the emergency helplines established for assistance and information.
The sudden flooding has affected normal life inseveral parts of Nepal, with Indian citizens also among those facing difficulties. Mr. Kharge appealed to Indians in Nepal, as well as their relatives in India, to contact the helplines without delay if they need assistance, information or help in establishing communication with family members.
The emergency helpline numbers are +977 985 131 6807, +977 970 910 7500 and +977 981 032 6117. All three numbers are also accessible through WhatsApp, according to a release by Home Minister.
CM speaks to survivor
Meanwhile, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar spoke to a survivor of the Nepal floods from Karnataka over a video call and assured him of the State government’s support and safety.
Mr. Shivakumar, who is currently in New Delhi, spoke to Mallinath and enquired about his condition following the tragedy. A video shared by the Chief Minister in social media showed him speaking with Mallinath and checking on his well-being.
During the conversation, Mr. Mallinath recalled that the flash floods had struck the same location where he had been a mere 10 minutes earlier. Mr. Shivakumar advised him to stay put for some more time and not be in a rush to leave, as he was in a safe area.
The Chief Minister also informed Mr. Mallinath that Karnataka officials were still unable to establish contact with some other tourists from the State who were in Nepal.
The Karnataka government, meanwhile, has stepped up efforts to identify residents of the State who may have been stranded in Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region (TAR) amid flash floods and disruptions reported along the Nepal-Tibet border and surrounding areas.
The Revenue Department, through the State Emergency Operation Centre (SEOC), has appealed to stranded individuals, their family members and tour operators to provide details through a Google Form at the earliest. The information will help the State government coordinate with the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), the Embassy of India in Nepal and the Embassy of India in Beijing for rescue, evacuation and other necessary assistance, according to a release by the revenue department.

stories.headline: How Karnataka’s Parks and BMLTA amendments may shield Tunnel Road project | Explained
stories.deck: The groups opposing the Tunnel Road project say that at the core of the two new amendments is an agenda to shield the project, against which three Public Interest Litigations (PILs) are currently being heard in court.
stories.bodyText:
Story so far: The Karnataka government passed two bills — the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, and the Bengaluru Metropolitan Land Transport Authority (Amendment) Bill, 2026 (BMLTA) — in the recently concluded Monsoon Session.
Both bills were passed without a single debate as the opposition alliance of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Janata Dal (Secular) was vehemently protesting against the inclusion of scam-accused B. Nagendra in the newly inducted ministers.
The bills are now being viewed in the context of the controversial Tunnel Road project, which is one of Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar’s pet projects. The Parks Bill, in particular, has drawn substantial backlash from the public, civic activists, and environmentalists. In addition, progressive thinkers and Kannada writers have also issued statements urging the government to repeal the amendments. Pressure is now mounting from various sections of society.
The groups opposing the project say that at the core of these amendments is an agenda to shield the Tunnel Road project, against which three Public Interest Litigations (PILs) are currently being heard in court. The PIL petitioners have alleged that the amendments defeat the points raised in the petitions.
What does the new Park amendment seek?
The amendment changes the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975, so that the State government can legally take or use a limited portion of land, which is 5%, inside protected government parks and gardens for public infrastructure and public-utility projects. The 1975 Act was originally designed to protect government parks and gardens from being diverted to other uses.
Section 4 of the 1975 Act restricts the use or alienation of land covered by the Act. However, Section 5 was included to make “specific exceptions.” In the past, all these exceptions have been project-specific permissions written into the law.
For example, the existing Section 5 lists six specific projects, including the use of Indira Gandhi Musical Fountain Park for road widening and Lalbagh for a metro station. Similarly, there have been additions related to Cubbon Park.
So, historically, the section dealt with specific parcels and specific projects.
What does the 2026 amendment change?
The present amendment replaces that largely project-specific approach with a general statutory mechanism, under which a committee set up by the government itself will assess the need for alienation.
The present amendment says that the government can use or alienate up to 5% of the total area of a park covered by the Act. “Alienation” can mean sale, lease, gift, exchange, and mortgage. However, there are restrictions on who can receive the land. The amendment says only the following can receive the land: a state government department, a statutory authority, a government company, or a local authority.
So, the amendment will not allow the government to hand over park land to private developers or private companies. This is exactly where activists feel that it is being used to shield the Tunnel Road project.
As a gatekeeping mechanism, the amendment makes it mandatory for a committee headed by an Additional Chief Secretary-level officer, along with officers and domain experts, to make recommendations before the government exercises the power to use 5% of the land.
The committee will make recommendations, and only after considering those recommendations can the State government decide that the proposed use is in “public interest.” What the Bill does not specify, however, is what constitutes “public interest” and who determines whether something is in “public interest.”
Another concern is that the term “public utility” is not clearly defined in the Bill. There are several unanswered questions in the form of loopholes: How is “public interest” defined? How is the area calculated where a park has already lost land? Can multiple projects cumulatively use the entire 5%? What happens to the land if the project is abandoned? Can leased land subsequently be transferred?
What is its connection with the Tunnel Road project?
The controversial Tunnel Road project needs about an acre of land in Lalbagh permanently and a few more acres temporarily during the construction period. In addition, there is a massive civic uproar against the project, with opponents claiming that it will have a severe impact on the city’s lakes and green cover, as well as historically important structures such as the 3-billion-year-old Peninsular Gneiss in Lalbagh.
While both Mr. Shivakumar and B.S. Prahallad, technical director of BSMILE, the implementing agency, have assured on multiple occasions that Lalbagh will not face any impact, fears among people about the destruction of the historic botanical garden still linger. The same fear has resulted in frequent silent protests in Lalbagh.
As soon as the Parks Bill passed through the Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council, citizens and activists were quick to draw connections, pointing out that the Bill, if it becomes an Act, would overcome the legal hurdles that the government could face in acquiring park land. The connection became more evident when the government also passed the BMLTA Bill, which essentially shields Tunnel Road projects from obtaining required permissions from competent agencies and could also help overcome major legal hurdles.
What is even more concerning is that about 65 acres of park land could now be at risk, as the city has over 1,350 acres of park land. With the new amendment, the government gets the authority to use 5% of the land with only one layer of scrutiny.
What is the BMLTA Act, and what is the amendment?
First, the Bengaluru Metropolitan Land Transport Authority (BMLTA) Act, 2022, created an authority intended to coordinate Bengaluru’s urban transport system. Under Section 19, the BMLTA has the power to approve major urban transport projects and ensure that they are consistent with the city’s Comprehensive Mobility Plan (CMP).
Section 19(2) says that a State government authority, agency, or department cannot start any public, private, or public-private partnership (PPP) urban mobility projects without prior approval from the BMLTA.
BMLTA approval is also required before seeking government financial assistance, including state budgetary allocations, externally aided funding, and central government-sponsored funding.
Essentially, on paper, the BMLTA is supposed to act as a gatekeeper for major urban transport projects. So, what is the problem with the 2026 amendment?
Essentially, there is a gap between the BMLTA Act coming into force in 2022 and the BMLTA Rules being notified in 2026. The government is now saying, through this amendment, that projects initiated during this gap period — between 2022 and 2026 — should not become legally questionable merely because the detailed BMLTA Rules had not yet been notified. The 2026 amendment, through Section 19(5), gives retrospective statutory protection to Bengaluru urban transport projects initiated between 2022 and 2026.
During that intervening period, Bengaluru continued to see projects being planned, initiated, and processed administratively. This also includes Tunnel Roads, Sancharayukta, and the Short Tunnel at Hebbal, among others, whose total value is over ₹1.1 lakh crore.
Earlier this year, the State government issued a draft of the BMLTA Rules, in which Rule 24 incorporated the savings clause, which also said that projects initiated between 2022 and 2026 would be exempted. However, this drew widespread criticism. Now, the clause is being made an amendment under Section 19(5).
How will it shield the Tunnel Road project?
The Tunnel Road project has been opposed, and three PILs have been filed against it in court and are being heard. According to the petitioners, the strong contentions in these PILs concern BMLTA approval and the loss of green cover.
The petitioners say the amendment is intended to accommodate the “sacrosanct projects” and could defeat whatever points they have raised in their petitions.
Dattatraya T. Devare, an environmental activist who is also a petitioner, said that laws were now being amended to defend the case against the Tunnel Road project in the Karnataka High Court.
“The petitioners have raised objections to the Tunnel Road project based on a review of the ambit of the existing laws. Now, such laws are being amended. This move is purely to escape from the petitions against both the long and short tunnels,” Mr. Devare told The Hindu.
He further expressed concern that opposition to the proposed infrastructure projects was either being ignored or defeated through amendments, citing the recent reduction of buffer zones along drains to accommodate roads along the buffer zones.
The move to amend the Bills is now being questioned, and several representations have been submitted to Governor Thaawar Chand Gehlot, expressing opposition and urging him to send the Bills back to the legislature. Retired bureaucrats such as A. Ravindra, former Forest Secretary A.N. Yellappa Reddy, and several others have opposed the amendments.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru mourns man behind Malleswaram's iconic idlis
briefs.deck: Veena Stores founder SD Suryanarayana Hegde passed away at eighty-seven years old. He established the popular Bengaluru eatery in nineteen seventy-seven after financial troubles. The establishment became an institution known for its idlis and special chutney. Many people, including celebrities, paid tribute to Hegde online after his passing. The beloved store continues to be a cherished landmark…
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Its fluffy idlis and chutney were favourites with Bollywood actor 
Deepika Padukone
. So, when Veena Stores in Bengaluru's Malleswaram announced the death of its founder, SD Suryanarayana Hegde, on Instagram earlier this week, Padukone was among those who paid her respects online.
In a city where idlis and vadas are staples, Hegde still managed to turn his store into an institution. Students from nearby schools and colleges, families, daily-wage workers, delivery partners, old residents and NRIs have all returned to Veena Stores for breakfast, making a visit there almost a ritual.
Hegde, who passed away at 87, started with a small condiment and coffee-tea store on Margosa Road in 1977, after his hotel had to be sold because of financial troubles. He named the new venture after his daughter, Veena.
When the store first opened, coffee, tea, badam milk and condiments were its primary offerings, while idli was almost a sideshow. Over the years, however, the idli — accompanied by generous helpings of chutney doled out from a bucket — became the star.
Today, Veena Stores has expanded, but the original hole-in-the-wall outlet remains etched in memory. “My home was just behind Veena Stores and my father and Hegde were friends. 
I used to call it thatha’s (grandfather’s) shop. In the 1980s, my friends and I would go there to eat after playing. Their speciality was, and still is, the chutney. The addition of mint to the chutney and its watery texture is what makes it special. Back then, more than idli, we used to eat chutney,” said Anand Raj, founder of Eat Raja in Malleswaram.
Raj remembers Hegde as a quiet man who usually sat at the cash register. “Now we have to buy a token and eat; back then, we would just eat whatever we wanted and go and tell him. He would accordingly tell us how much to pay. I also remember him frying vadas in the kitchen. Its crispy texture would immediately tempt us. The store is the pride of Malleswaram,” he said.
Suchitra Deep, founder of Malleswaram Social, describes the store as a landmark. “I’m sure Hegde would not have thought that the small shop he founded would become this institution. Both he and Pradeep, his son, were at it for years,” she said.
Deep remembers visiting the store around two decades ago, when the crowds outside made getting to the counter itself a challenge. “Even though they operated in a limited window, they were very efficient,” she said. “What I will always remember is the hole-in-the-wall outlet and the fact that they had the most amazing vadas and chutney. Nobody made vade like them.”

briefs.headline: 2 women steal 4 gold bangles worth Rs 12 lakh from showroom in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Two women posing as customers visited a Malabar Gold and Diamonds jewellery showroom on 
MG Road
 and stole four gold bangles worth Rs 12 lakh. The theft was discovered during stock check at the end of the day.
The showroom manager told police the two unidentified “customers” were being assisted by a saleswoman, who was showing them bangles from a display tray at 3.15pm on Aug 22.
When the sales executive was busy choosing designs to show them, one of the women allegedly picked up two bangles and slipped them into her handbag. She repeated the act moments later, taking two more bangles from the tray before leaving the counter. The women claimed they didn’t like the designs and left the showroom.
The theft came to light during the showroom’s daily stock verification. Police said CCTV footage has captured the registration number of the suspects’ vehicle.
A senior police officer said a case has been registered under BNS Section 305 (theft in a dwelling house, or means of transportation or place of worship, etc).

briefs.headline: Lalbagh legend Krumbiegel’s tombstone damaged in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: The tombstone of Gustav Krumbiegel, the legendary landscape architect credited with shaping parts of Lalbagh Botanical Garden, has been found severely damaged at Hosur Road cemetery. Heritage activists have demanded an investigation and immediate restoration.
Heritage Beku said the damaged headstone, located at gate 1, plot 6, row 7, grave 6 of the cemetery, represents a significant loss to the city’s cultural and historical heritage. “Krumbiegel’s contributions to Bangalore’s landscape, particularly his iconic design work at Lalbagh, are invaluable to our city’s heritage,” read a letter by the citizens’ group addressed to city police and horticulture department.
Heritage Beku group led by Priya Chetty Rajagopal sought a joint inspection by police and horticulture department to ascertain the cause of damage and determine whether it resulted from an accident, natural wear and tear or deliberate vandalism.
If vandalism is established, the activists have demanded police investigation to identify those responsible. They also urged horticulture department to undertake urgent professional restoration of the tombstone.
The letter said Alyia Krumbiegel, Gustav’s great-granddaughter and core member of Heritage Beku, expressed grief over the damage.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru roads get Rs 8,000 crore boost; potholes to be fixed by Sept-end
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) will take up road improvement works covering around 2,500km at an estimated cost of Rs 8,000 crore over the next six months, city development minister Krishna Byre Gowda said Thursday.
The works will include asphalt resurfacing and white-topping, with around 250km already completed. The minister said tenders for white-topping should be awarded by Dec and directed officials to expedite the works while maintaining quality.
He also ordered a survey of potholes on all arterial and sub-arterial roads using camera-mounted vehicles and directed officials to complete repairs by the end of Sept. “Once potholes on the major roads are addressed, the focus will shift to ward roads,” he said.
Byre Gowda also announced monthly reviews of civic works and grievances by him, the department’s additional chief secretary and the GBA chief commissioner. Since GBA was formed, 75,152 complaints have been registered through Sahaaya 2.0, of which 73,985 have been addressed.
If an issue persists, senior officers will re-audit complaints marked as resolved and will be given targets for reviewing them. Potholes, garbage and streetlights remain the major categories of grievances, he said.

briefs.headline: 13 Karnataka residents stranded, 4 NRI pilgrims missing: Chief minister’s office
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 At least 13 
Karnataka
 residents, including 11 from Bengaluru Urban district, are stranded in Nepal and Tibet Autonomous Region following flash floods, while four Bengaluru-origin Kannadigas living in the US and travelling on 
Kailash Mansarovar Yatra
 remain untraceable, the state govt said Thursday.
According to the chief minister’s office, the state emergency operations centre has compiled details of the stranded residents — 11 are from Bengaluru Urban, one from Mysuru, and one from Dharwad district. Most of them are at Timure in Nepal’s Rasuwa district, while a few are in Darchen in Tibet Autonomous Region. They are part of larger groups that include people from other states.
Details of the stranded residents are being shared with the rapid response cells of the ministry of external affairs and Indian missions in Kathmandu and Beijing.
Four Bengaluru-origin NRI Kannadigas who travelled from the US to Nepal for the Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimage have also been reported missing. They had visited the Chinese embassy in the flood-affected area on Aug 26, but have since not contacted friends and family. Their friends approached the state disaster management authority, providing details and seeking help in tracing them.
The authority said it has established contact with two Karnataka residents stranded in floods, Mallinath Kolakundi and Sangamesh Kanakapura, both from Chincholi taluk in Kalaburagi district. Chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
 spoke to Mallinath over a video call and enquired about his well-being. Mallinath said he was a fan of Shivakumar and a devotee of God.
For assistance, people can contact the state emergency operations centre at 1070 or 080 22253707, or send an email to seockarnataka@gmail.com.

briefs.headline: Parents missing in Tibet, daughters wait anxiously in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 As news of the flash floods broke, gloom settled over a city home where two children, along with other family members, waited anxiously for a call or message from their parents, who have been missing since Wednesday in 
Tibet
 Autonomous Region.
The two were among a group of 77 pilgrims from Isha Foundation who were returning from Kailash Mansarovar Yatra and were at Gyirong immigration centre in Tibet when flash floods struck.
The two, both in their early 40s, live in Florida, United States. “They had come to Bengaluru to drop off their daughters — aged 13 and 15 — at a relative’s place and then left for the pilgrimage. We learnt they had reached the immigration centre at 9.05am. After that, there has been no communication,” a family member said.
The family said the couple’s last mobile activity indicated they were at the immigration centre when disaster struck. They later received confirmation from Isha Foundation that the group was present at the centre.

briefs.headline: Big ticket infrastructure projects or white elephants?
briefs.deck: The Karnataka government is pushing for projects worth nearly ₹1.5 lakh crore in and around Bengaluru, which activists argue are ‘vanity projects’ being built exclusively for cars. Are they worth being tolled or is it a case of the poor subsidising the rich? Chetan B.C. and K.V. Aditya Bharadwaj explore...
briefs.bodyText:
After a two-decade lull, barring the slow-moving Namma Metro, the Karnataka government is now pushing for several big ticket infrastructure projects in and around Bengaluru worth nearly ₹1.5 lakh crore.
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar has been talking of building “New Bengalurus” on the back of these big ticket infra-projects. These include two twin-tunnel roads and 13 elevated corridors criss-crossing the city, Peripheral Ring Road (PRR) around the city, and Live-Work-Play townships in Bidadi and near Doddaballapur.
Almost all the projects are facing opposition either from land owners resisting acquisition of their land or by civic activists arguing these are “white elephants” and “vanity projects” being built exclusively for cars. There are multiple petitions challenging the tunnel road project in the High Court of Karnataka and the National Green Tribunal on various grounds, including statutory non-compliance, damage to the environment, etc.
But what has gone below the radar is how most of these road projects will be heavily tolled. The two twin-tunnel projects, four long flyovers cutting across the city, and the PRR will be tolled, making the commute expensive and exclusive for those who can afford it.
On the other hand, the State is not investing directly in these projects. Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) like Bengaluru Business Corridor Ltd. and Bengaluru Smart Infrastructure Ltd. (B-SMILE) set up by the State have raised huge loans to fund them and the State has only given sovereign guarantee. Barring PRR-funded entirely through a Housing and Urban Development Corporation Ltd. (HUDCO) loan of ₹27,000 crore, the rest of the projects have private investments, but not fully. These SPVs have again raised loans to give Viability Gap Funding of 40% for twin-tunnels and two flyovers, while the other two will be built entirely by private players.
Activists argue that this means that public money is being pumped in to build infrastructure solely for the rich.
Exorbitant toll
While the toll structure for the rest of the projects is not in the public domain yet, the estimated toll in the 16.7 km long North-South Twin-Tunnel Road between Hebbal and Silk Board is pegged at ₹19 per km in the Detailed Project Report (DPR). This means a one-way trip will cost ₹317, and nearly ₹650 for a round trip. Only cars and buses are likely to be allowed.
This toll structure, part of the DPR, is for the project estimated to cost ₹17,700 crore, which according to B.S. Prahallad, Technical Director, B-SMILE, may go up to ₹20,000 crore with the inclusion of utilities and other factors. However, Adani Enterprises Ltd., which has emerged as the lowest bidder, has quoted over ₹22,000 crore for the project, which is still under evaluation.
This cost escalation even before the contract is awarded could mean the toll structure when the road is finally open for traffic after a four-year construction period could be much higher.
For comparison, a km of autorickshaw ride in Bengaluru today costs ₹18 and a km of cab ride is at ₹24. The toll charges alone for a trip in the tunnel road will be much higher as the commuter will also bear the fuel charges.
“Leave alone someone poor, two-wheelers and three-wheelers are not even allowed inside the tunnel roads. Even for a middle-class car owner like me, the proposed toll is very exorbitant,” says N.S. Mukunda, one of the petitioners challenging the project in the High Court of Karnataka.
Other projects
The draft DPR of the East-West Tunnel, spanning 19.2 km, has estimated a construction cost of ₹ 30,000 crore. The Special Purpose Vehicle will likely spend ₹1,500 crore per km of the East-West Tunnel.
A total of 13 elevated corridors, spanning 120.1 km, will cost ₹22,234.99 crore. Of them, the State will build nine flyovers of less than 10 km each at a cost of ₹4,755 crore and it will not be tolled.
Two other flyovers of 28 km and 18.50 km, at a cost of ₹7,577 crore, will be built with 40% Viability Gap Funding and 60% private investment like tunnel roads. Two other flyovers spanning 17.3 km and 27.2 km at a total cost of ₹9,902 crore will be completely built by the private concessionaire. These projects will be tolled for at least 20 years.
According to Mr. Prahallad, the plan is to set the toll charges at ₹10 per km for cars and ₹7 per km for two-wheelers. This will also mean that for a car user, commuting on the 28-km-long flyover connecting Yeshwantpur and K.R. Puram will cost ₹280 one-way, if there is no escalation further.
The Bengaluru Business Corridor (BBC) has taken up the construction of the 68-km-long PRR Phase I, raising a loan of ₹27,000 crore from HUDCO. This road will also be tolled, though the toll structure is yet to be determined.
‘Poor subsidising the rich’
Mr. Prahallad argued that providing less-traffic expressways on toll is a practice across the world and that non-tolled alternatives will anyway continue to exist for those who do not want to pay.
However, what complicates this argument is the fact that the State is paying a 40% Viability Gap Funding for most of these projects and the State is funding the PRR completely all by itself. Only two flyovers are entirely funded by the concessionaire.
Economist Narendar Pani said the use of public money as Viability Gap Funding for these projects meant those who cannot afford to pay the toll and use the road pay for the infrastructure. “Especially since we are dependent on indirect taxes than direct taxes, even the poor are taxed and their money is being used to build infrastructure for the rich,” he said.
“Given the shortage of resources, has the government done an analysis of the necessity of this spending in the form of Viability Gap Funding. Such an evaluation should analyse the returns on these investments. Evidently, no such evaluation has happened. Many talk of welfare schemes as freebies to the poor, but these projects are essentially freebies for the rich,” Prof. Pani said.
Advocate and activist Vinay Sreenivasa, a petitioner challenging the tunnel road project in the NGT, said that public money for road projects where we need to further pay hefty tolls to ply on, “amounts to the poor subsidising the rich”. “We have been demanding a similar Viability Gap Funding for Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC) to make buses cheap and viable. It may even be a fraction of what Viability Gap Funding is being paid to these car-centric white elephant projects. But the government never gives it to BMTC and it is opposed by many saying BMTC must be self-sustaining. Why this double standard?” he asked.
The core of the problem is the exorbitant costs of these projects and the small fraction of the population it serves. One of the PILs flags this issue. “It is manifestly arbitrary as it costs ₹1,000 crore per km (versus ₹433 crore/km for Mumbai Coastal Road, ₹300 crore/km for Delhi Metro) while benefitting only 2.7% of the population (car owners)”, the petition says. However, the estimated cost of drilling a kilometre of tunnel road in North-South corridor is pegged at ₹1,170 crore and likely to go up to ₹1,500 crore for the East-West corridor.
Given the project exclusively permits four-wheelers while prohibiting two-wheelers (around 82% of the city’s 1.07 crore vehicles) and autorickshaws, it creates economic apartheid in public infrastructure funded by all taxpayers, the petition argues.
Ashish Verma, convener, IISc Sustainable Transportation Lab, said none of these projects are backed by data or have scientific basis to act as a traffic solution. All grade separators only shift the bottleneck and network travel times only get worse. “With such high tolls, they will end up becoming ‘VIP green corridors’ for the rich, funded by all of us, even as it worsens traffic in the city,” he said.
Srikanth Vishwanathan, CEO, Janaagraha Centre for Citizenship and Democracy, and an expert in municipal finance, said most of these projects were both poor use of public finance and planning choices. “Actually, these are ad-hoc projects with no planning to talk of,” he added. “Either there has to be no Viability Gap Funding or no toll. You can’t have both,” he argued.
There are other concerns as well. B-SMILE has pledged the city’s advertisement and Premium FAR revenues to repay the loan taken towards the Viability Gap Funding of the tunnel roads project. “Future revenues of the corporations cannot be pledged by a parastatal. This is a violation of the autonomy of the municipal bodies, especially when there are no elected councils for six years now,” Mr. Srikanth said.
Can city roads be tolled?
Usually only State and National Highways outside city limits are tolled, and not roads inside the city. As of today, no road, barring parts of NICE Road within the city limits, in the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) area is tolled. Even when private concessionaires have built roads like the International Airport Expressway within the city limits, the toll gate is outside the GBA area.
The tunnel roads and the four elevated corridors proposed to be developed by B-SMILE will be the first tolled roads within the GBA area. But can roads in the city be tolled?
Toll collection in the State is governed under the Karnataka Road User Fee (Determination of Rates and Collection) Rules, 2013, which states that a toll plaza should normally be located more than 10 km away from the boundary of a municipality or town.
But there are two exceptions. First, it can be closer than 10 km, given the executing authority can permit a toll plaza within 10 km of the town boundary if it records reasons in writing.
The exception that the B-smile is depending on is the second one - that “a toll plaza can be within 5 km or even inside the town where a section of a State Highway or a standalone structure is built primarily for the use of residents of that town or municipal area”. In that situation, the toll plaza can be located within the municipal/town limits, or even within 5 km of those limits.
Here, the elevated corridor itself becomes a structure “specifically” being constructed for the residents of the town, which gives B-SMILE the authority to collect toll, Mr. Prahallad argued. He explained the rationale behind the toll stating that it is a structure that will connect two different parts of the city and it saves a good amount of time.
This comes even as the High Court of Karnataka recently observed that the Bangalore-Mysore Infrastructure Corridor (BMIC) project “appears to be one of the biggest scams in the State”. Saying it was fit case for an independent assessment and investigation, it expressed doubt about the conduct of such a probe “as the State itself is accomplice in allowing the project proponents (Nandi Infrastructure Corridor Enterprises and others) to earn huge profits illegally” by a host of means including “collecting huge toll in violation of the Frame Work Agreement”.
Ever since, former Chief Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy has been demanding that the State government take over NICE Road and immediately stop toll collection from road users on the stretch. The Congress government hasn’t responded yet to this specific demand. The issue was expected to come up for debate in the recent Karnataka Legislature session, which was a washout and no meaningful debate took place as the Opposition BJP demanded the resignation of a Minister and the government did not yield.

briefs.headline: India to host Brazil, Panama, Uruguay for football friendlies
briefs.deck: The matches against Brazil and Uruguay will be played at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan in Kolkata and the match against Panama will be played at the Kanteerava Stadium in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
India will host two-time World Cup champions Uruguay for a football friendly on October 6 in Kolkata, the third international match the country will play at home against quality teams in the upcoming FIFA window.
The match will be played three days after India's international friendly against five-time World Cup champions Brazil at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan in Kolkata. The match against Uruguay will also be played at the same iconic venue.
The Indian team is also playing against Panama at the Kanteerava Stadium in Bengaluru on September 26.
The FIFA international window is from September 21 to October 6 and a country can play a maximum of four matches in this period.
"The Indian men's national team will welcome another heavyweight of world football to Kolkata, with two-time FIFA World Cup champions Uruguay set to face India in an international friendly match at Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan on October 6, 2026. The fixture will be India's third high-profile international friendly of the window," the All India Football Federation (AIFF) said in a statement on Thursday.
"La Celeste's arrival in Kolkata adds another major fixture to an unprecedented run of international football for Indian fans, with three World Cup-playing nations — Panama, Brazil and Uruguay — set to visit the country within the same FIFA window."
Uruguay are currently ranked 20th in the FIFA chart. They won the World Cup in 2030 and 1950, and reached the semifinals three times — 1954, 1970 and 2010.
In the 2026 World Cup, they made a group stage exit, after playing out draws against Saudi Arabia (1-1) and Cape Verde (2-2), and losing to eventual champions Spain (0-1).
They were also eliminated in the group stage in the 2022 World Cup.
The current head coach of Uruguay, Diego Forlan, played for Mumbai City FC in 2016.
Earlier in the day, the AIFF announced that Sree Kanteerava Stadium in Bengaluru will host India's international friendly against Panama on September 26.
The fixture will mark the Blue Tigers' first appearance in Bengaluru since their SAFF Championship 2023 campaign, when India lifted the title on home soil after defeating Kuwait in the final at the same venue.
Panama are currently ranked 44th in the world. They featured in the 2026 World Cup in the Americas and were eliminated in the group stage after losing to Ghana (0-1), Croatia (0-1) and England (0-2). They also took part in the 2018 World Cup and bowed out in the group stage.
The Blue Tigers are also slated to face New Zealand on November 12 and 15 in away matches.

stories.headline: Assam initiates plan to streamline agarwood industry
stories.deck: The State government has proposed a series of measures to simplify regulations, strengthen cultivation and processing, and facilitate exports
stories.bodyText:
GUWAHATI
The Assam Government has decided to streamline and expand its agarwood industry, proposing several measures to simplify regulations, strengthen cultivation and processing, and facilitate exports.
These measures were discussed at the first meeting of the Assam Agarwood Task Force and agarwood stakeholders in Guwahati on August 26.
Agarwood is dark, fragrant, resinous heartwood that comes from trees in the genus Aquilaria. These trees have pale, light, and odourless wood, but produce resin when infected by Phaeoacremonium parasitica. This resin yields high-value perfumes.
The meeting brought together agarwood growers, processors, entrepreneurs, traders, exporters, scientists, and researchers.
According to Bimal Bora, Assam’s Industries and Commerce Minister, a key proposal was to establish a systematic mechanism to register agarwood plantations cultivated outside forest areas, accompanied by an awareness campaign to ensure growers understand the regulatory requirements.
“The stakeholders proposed removing agarwood chip and oil processing units from the conventional wood-based industry framework, arguing that cultivated agarwood and its processing have distinct characteristics and requirements,” he said.
Another recommendation was to simplify the issuance of certificates of origin for agarwood cultivated outside forest areas and beyond the prescribed forest proximity zone. In such cases, the certificate could be issued through the District Commissioner or Circle Officer instead of requiring the District Forest Officer-level process in every instance.
“We also discussed removing or reviewing registration fees imposed on cultivated agarwood trees by the Forest Department to encourage farmers to register plantations and bring more of the sector into the formal economy,” Mr. Bora said.
Faster testing
The task force proposed establishing agarwood chip and oil testing facilities at the district level to improve quality assessment and authentication while reducing trade delays.
The stakeholders called for a time-bound mechanism for CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora) and Directorate General of Foreign Trade permissions, with eligible applications proposed to be processed within 15 days, subject to fulfilment of statutory requirements.
The measures seek to create a transparent and predictable export system that would allow genuine growers, processors, and exporters in Assam to access international markets more efficiently.
The stakeholders recommended that the Centre consider stopping or substantially restricting imports of agarwood, agarwood chips, oil, and related raw materials, subject to national laws, international obligations, and environmental safeguards.
The proposal is intended to strengthen India’s domestic agarwood industry, reduce dependence on imported material, and encourage greater investment in cultivation and processing. Stakeholders also stressed the need for safeguards against illegal harvesting, smuggling, and market disruption.
The stakeholders hoped that Wednesday’s meeting would lay the foundation for transforming Assam’s agarwood sector into a regulated, farmer-friendly, sustainable, and globally competitive industry.
“With scientific testing, simplified certification, streamlined regulations, and faster export procedures, the State government aims to position Assam as a major hub for agarwood and Oud-based products,” Finance and Forest Minister Jayanta Mallabaruah, who attended the meeting with Agriculture Minister Pijush Hazarika, said.
The other participants included Chief Secretary Ravi Kota, Special Chief Secretary M.K. Yadava, and Additional Chief Secretary J.B. Ekka. Representatives from the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region, CHEMEXCIL, Fragrance and Flavour Development Centre, CSIR- North East Institute of Science and Technology, Rain Forest Research Institute, Fragrance and Flavour Association, and Sugandh Vyapar Sangh also participated.

stories.headline: ECLGS 5.0 support for MSMEs to last only for the allocated guarantee cover
stories.deck: All its member lending institutions have been asked to sanction loans under the ECLGS 5.0 to MSMEs and non-MSMEs and apply for credit guarantee under the scheme as it will be considered on first come first served basis subject the availability of guarantee cover
stories.bodyText:
The National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company (NCGTC) has informed banks that the Emergency Credit Linked Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) 5.0, which was announced in May this year to support MSMEs and non-MSMEs affected by the West Asia war, will be implemented only as long as the ₹2.5 lakh crore guarantee cover is reached.
All its member lending institutions have been asked to sanction loans under the ECLGS 5.0 to MSMEs and non-MSMEs and apply for credit guarantee under the scheme as it will be considered on first come first served basis subject the availability of guarantee cover. “Any sanction beyond available guarantee cover shall not be admissible under the scheme”, it told the banks in a communication dated August 18, 2026.
The credit guarantees issued to MSMEs and non-MSMEs (except domestic airlines) will not exceed ₹2.5 lakh crore, it pointed out.
In an earlier communication issued on August 3, the NCGTC asked the banks to stop supporting non-MSMEs under the scheme as a substantial portion of the approved outlay was already used. Since the scheme was intended to ensure credit availability to MSMEs, fresh sanctions for non-MSMEs should not be taken up with immediate effect. All lending institutions should stop processing non-MSME loans under the ECLGS 5.0 and remaining amount would be for MSMEs, it said.
When the scheme was announced, it was to be implemented till the end of March next year.
Meanwhile, the Union Finance Ministry sought suggestions from some of the MSME associations on finance and credit support required for the MSMEs. President of the Coimbatore District Small Industries Association V. Rangaswamy said the Association has suggested increasing working capital and overdraft limits to 40 % of turnover and interest subvention support. “We need credit support as raw material prices have increased 100 % and payment cycles are stretched. The government should extend the ECLGS with another ₹2.1 lakh crore credit guarantee cover,” he said.
