stories.headline: Sensex opens 200 points higher, Nifty hovers around 24,000 ahead of Fed chair’s address
stories.bodyText:
SEBI issued the consultation paper on August 27 and has invited public comments on the draft circular until September 17.
If finalised, the proposed provisions would come into effect "with immediate effect", according to the draft circular.
All other provisions under Chapter V of the Non-Convertible Securities (NCS) Master Circular would remain unchanged.
Under the draft framework, the debt securities covered by the exemption would have to meet additional safeguards aimed at limiting the provision to relatively lower-risk instruments.
The securities would have to be unsubordinated or senior and secured by a first or pari passu charge over identifiable assets of the issuer. They would also need to carry a minimum AA- rating on the date of the private placement.
SEBI said the conditions were intended to ensure that the exemption applied only to instruments with relatively lower risk.
The regulator said the proposal was also based on the view that "sufficient information about the issuer is already available in public domain", given that listed companies are subject to regulatory oversight and disclosure requirements.
The issuer would have to be registered with or regulated by a financial-sector regulator in India and listed on a recognised stock exchange for at least one year. At the time of granting in-principle approval, the stock exchange would also have to confirm that there were no pending SEBI or exchange fines or penalties relating to applicable LODR compliance.
The issuer must also have recorded no defaults during the previous three financial years or the current financial year on specified obligations, including repayments linked to debt securities, deposits, dividends and term loans. It would also have to submit an auditor's certificate to the stock exchange.
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has proposed exempting certain listed issuers from the mandatory appointment of a merchant banker when raising small-value debt through private placement, citing high costs, limited availability of merchant bankers and delays in execution.
Under the proposal, the exemption would cover debt securities or non-convertible redeemable preference shares issued through private placement with a face value of Rs 10,000, subject to specified eligibility conditions.
SEBI said market participants had raised concerns over the burden associated with appointing merchant bankers for such offerings. The consultation paper highlighted the "Disproportionate burden of the appointment cost", along with the limited number of merchant bankers operating in the debt segment and delays that could affect fundraising.
The quity markets opened higher after two consecutive sessions of losses, although investor caution remained ahead of a speech by Federal Reserve Chair and following sharp swings during the previous session's closing auction.
The Nifty 50 rose 0.13% to 24,122.60, while the BSE Sensex gained 0.25% to 77,128.05 at 9.15am IST.
Thirteen of the 16 major sectoral indices advanced in early trade. The broader market also opened firmer, with the small-cap and mid-cap indices rising 0.2% and 0.1%, respectively.
The benchmarks had fallen around 1% each over the previous two sessions and were on course for a third consecutive weekly decline. Elevated oil prices and higher US Treasury yields continued to weigh on global risk appetite.
Investor sentiment was also affected by Thursday's volatile closing auction, which coincided with the monthly derivatives expiry. Derivatives turnover on the BSE index was at its lowest level in 11 months for a monthly expiry session.
The indicative Sensex close briefly fell more than 3% during the closing auction before recovering some of the losses and eventually ending 0.7% lower.
Markets were therefore expected to remain volatile, with investors closely watching the Federal Reserve chair's remarks for clues on the US interest-rate outlook.

briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: In the first monthly expiry of derivatives contracts on BSE after the introduction of Closing Auction Session, popularly known as CAS, sensex and Bankex, BSE’s banking index, witnessed wild swings, triggering social media outcry. The sharp movement in indices and some of their constituents also gave rise to chances for some smart investors to make a killing.
On Aug 3, Sebi introduced CAS, a new process of discovering the closing price of stocks that is used in several developed markets, aimed at eliminating chances of price manipulation. CAS is now valid for all those 200-odd stocks on which equity derivatives contracts are traded. For the rest of the non-derivatives stocks, the old system of volume-weighted average price (VWAP) continues. Since the launch of CAS, however, the two leading indices—Nifty and sensex—have witnessed extreme volatility and wide price variation between 3.15pm, just before CAS starts every session, and 3.30pm, when it ends.
On Thursday, within a five-minute window after the start of CAS on BSE—between 3.18pm and 3.23pm—sensex crashed over 2,200 points.

It finally closed at 76,934 points, down 539 points from its Wednesday close.
On NSE, things were relatively quiet. Between 3.18pm and 3.22pm, Nifty slid over 100 points but then recovered about 60 points to close 117 points lower at 24,091 points. On BSE, some of the leading stocks which are also sensex constituents witnessed huge volatility. During CAS, Reliance Industries, which has the highest weight in sensex, slid from Rs 1,289 to Rs 1,250, a drop of 3% within seven minutes, but then recovered equally sharply to close at Rs 1,286. Traders continued to cry foul. On X (formerly Twitter), one trader pointed out that if someone had bought sensex put options of 76,500 worth Rs 1 lakh at 3.15pm and exited at 3.20pm, the trader’s profit in just five minutes would have been Rs 44 lakh.
A week ago, Copthall Mauritius, a JP Morgan arm, was caught by Sebi, manipulating sensex and its constituents and for making illegal gains worth nearly Rs 3 crore. Sebi had alleged that domestic broker, Mansi Stock & Share Broking, indulged in a similar manipulation strategy. The regulator has banned Copthall and Mansi Broking (for proprietary trades only) from the market and ordered the two to disgorge illegal gains worth nearly Rs 3.8 crore.

briefs.headline: HDFC looks to appeal 99.97% haircut on claims against Zee’s Chandra
briefs.deck: Assenting creditors (80.8%) contested allegations of being related parties and argued that Rs. 6.5-crore plan offered a better outcome compared to pushing the personal guarantor into bankruptcy, since Chandra’s net worth according to the resolution professional was only Rs. 31.8 crore, of which Rs. 25 crore was his mortgaged house. Chandra has disputed the Rs. 22,000-crore liability, stating it…
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: With the National Company Law Tribunal this week clearing a repayment plan offering only Rs. 6.5 crore in a case concerning Zee Group’s Subhash Chandra’s personal guarantees for loans taken by his companies, 
HDFC Bank
 said it is exploring an appeal.
Creditors filed claims of Rs. 22,006 crore against Subhash Chandra for the loans he backed, but the repayment plan approved by a majority of creditors and cleared by NCLT approves a 99.97% haircut — without impacting lender’s right to recover from the actual borrowers.
Assenting creditors (80.8%) contested allegations of being related parties and argued that Rs. 6.5-crore plan offered a better outcome compared to pushing the personal guarantor into bankruptcy, since Chandra’s net worth according to the resolution professional was only Rs. 31.8 crore, of which Rs. 25 crore was his mortgaged house. Chandra has disputed the Rs. 22,000-crore liability, stating it reflected historical claims filed in 2022.
‘Was only a guarantor, did not borrow’
Chandra put objecting creditors’ claims at Rs 3,992 crore, of which Rs 620 crore was settled, with borrowing entities offering another Rs 1,063–1,113 crore. The remaining Rs 16,201 crore of assenting claims was also being addressed by principal borrowers. 
He said he was only a personal guarantor and had not himself borrowed, adding that most of the guarantees were provided by him after group companies defaulted as lenders and made “emotional appeals” for guarantees, saying otherwise their employees would lose their jobs.
The assenting creditors said even after the settlement, principal borrowers (group companies) continued to remain on the hook.
HDFC’s Rs 698 crore claim represented 3.2% of the sum. Other dissenters, accounting for around 15%, include Axis Bank, Canara Bank, RBL Bank, Union Bank UK, IDBI Trusteeship and LIC Housing Finance.
LIC Housing Finance said the order does not affect borrowers’ corporate liabilities or its security.
The claims arise from Chandra’s personal guarantees for borrowings by Vivek Infracon, Spirit Textiles, and Churu Enterprises, as well as mortgage-backed facilities for Essel Corporate Resources and Jayneer Infrapower.
The dissenting lenders argued that assenting creditors Veena Investments, Direct Media Distribution Ventures, World Crest Advisors, Lemonade Capital Advisors, and Corpcall Capital Advisors were related or associate entities and controlled 61.8% to 62% of voting rights, making them ineligible under Section 109(4)(b) of the IBC. They cited Veena’s control by Sushila Devi Goel, wife of Jawahar Goel, the personal guarantor’s brother, and links between partners of Lemonade and Corpcall and companies disclosed as related parties in Veena’s accounts.
The 99.97% haircut headlines caught nationwide attention, with Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh stating: “The National Company Law Tribunal has just approved a repayment plan of a noted businessman under which creditors will receive only Rs 6.5 crores against admitted claims of around Rs 22,006.57 crore. This is not just a haircut. It is actually a mundan and makes a complete mockery of the 
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code
, 2016.”
In a post on X, Vijay Mallya said, “If true, many congratulations to my friend Subhash,” contrasting the outcome with his own case by claiming banks and the govt had recovered Rs 14,100 crore against a Rs 6,203 crore judgment debt while continuing to pursue him, signing off with “Indian Debt Resolution Justice”.

briefs.headline: Centre goes all-out to woo Japanese companies for investment
briefs.deck: India, officials said, is seen to be a reliable player, which has a democracy and rule of law, in addition to a large and growing market. The pitch is also that a base in India will also help tap the large talent pool as well as traditional trade relations with West Asia and Africa, which also boasts of a large Indian diaspora.
briefs.bodyText:
OSAKA: From focusing on high-tech industries to weaning away entities with presence in China and southeast Asia and wooing small Japanese banks, beyond the Big 3, that have strong local relationships, govt is deploying every tool to get Japanese firms to invest in India.
The moves come amid heightened distrust with China, which has not just stopped supply of critical inputs needed by the Japanese industry, but has also indicated that profits can’t be repatriated to Japan and need to be invested there.
India, officials said, is seen to be a reliable player, which has a democracy and rule of law, in addition to a large and growing market. The pitch is also that a base in India will also help tap the large talent pool as well as traditional trade relations with West Asia and Africa, which also boasts of a large Indian diaspora.
“We are working with the regional and smaller banks to work in India,” India’s ambassador to Japan Nagma M Mallik said, adding that govt is keen to attract Japanese SME investment, which works closely with these lenders.
A host of small players, from Yokohama Bank to The 77 Bank, Resona Bank and Toyoma Bank, operate in 47 prefectures, the first level of administration, and have close ties with local players. Many of the bankers also go on to be governors and wield influence. 
As a result, getting these banks can help open the doors to local businesses and SMEs, which are large in size compared to Indian standards and specialise in product segments.
While some of the small banks are sending researchers to India, who will work with the three large Japanese banks, MUFG, SMBC and Mizuho, which have now established local presence through acquisitions, said another official.
Separately, govt is hoping that just like Maruti brought in its vendors, the other large Japanese players will get its affiliates to set up shop in the country so that the entire value chain is covered.
Japan is the fifth largest investor in India and govt is hoping that it will move up given the recent rush of investments, which have been focused more on the financial sector.

briefs.headline: Gaana, Fenix360 tie up to boost engagement
briefs.deck: Streaming changed how the world listens to music. But for a long time, the relationship between artists and fans has largely stopped at the play button. Discovery happens on one platform, community happens on another and monetisation happens somewhere else if it happens at all. This partnership aims to close that gap. The wider ecosystem will also introduce new monetisation opportunities for…
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Gaana has partnered with social media and creator platform Fenix360 to build a more direct relationship between artists and their audiences by bringing content, community and commerce together within one ecosystem. At the centre of the integration will be a native scrolling social feed within Gaana, enabling artists to share visual content around their work while allowing fans to discover, follow and engage with them without having to move across multiple platforms.
Streaming changed how the world listens to music. But for a long time, the relationship between artists and fans has largely stopped at the play button. Discovery happens on one platform, community happens on another and monetisation happens somewhere else if it happens at all. This partnership aims to close that gap.
The wider ecosystem will also introduce new monetisation opportunities for artists. Through Fenix360’s tools, artists will be able to build digital storefronts, offer physical and digital merchandise, sell tickets to live shows, host gated and paid live streams, and receive direct financial support from their fans. A key part of the proposition is Fenix360’s creator-first monetisation model, under which artists will retain 70% of the revenue generated through its monetisation tools.

briefs.headline: ‘Govt to focus on easing processes to boost FDI’
briefs.deck: Goyal said govt was keen that investment model should not only focus on large companies but the entire value chain that leads to downstream indigenisation. In paints, for instance, import of titanium dioxide, a key input, is of the tune of $1 billion and govt wants it to be manufactured in India, he said.
briefs.bodyText:
Commerce & industry minister Piyush Goyal Thursday said govt will focus on easing processes and faster clearances, wherever required, to boost FDI flows, while asserting that Indian economy has seen a robust expansion in first quarter, for which data is due to be released next week.
Focus on value chain, KYC
“We are open to ideas, whatever industry demands… there’s tremendous scope to improve process, procedure and policy to help faster flow of FDI and to help give comfort to investors about the fact that their investments will lead to production and productive activity faster,” the minister said. He added that faster and more efficient KYC norms and mutual recognition agreements with regulators from other countries are required so that approvals on both sides are recognised and there could be some areas for simplification.
Goyal said govt was keen that investment model should not only focus on large companies but the entire value chain that leads to downstream indigenisation. In paints, for instance, import of titanium dioxide, a key input, is of the tune of $1 billion and govt wants it to be manufactured in India, he said.
Similarly, the idea is to go beyond semiconductors and promote production of gases, specialty chemicals, equipment, components, so that the value chain goes beyond design and testing or assembly.
“So, our effort is more and more going deep dive, becoming self-reliant, and also creating more jobs.”
No decision on CPTPP, focus on FTAs
Goyal has pitched India’s FTAs as an opportunity for investors to make use of and export to other countries, in addition to making in India for domestic market. While stating that more FTAs – from Canada and Chile to Israel and the South African Customs Union -- are under negotiation, he said there is no decision on Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) – the 11-nation trading bloc that includes Japan, Australia, Canada, Chile, Malaysia and Singapore. “A lot of people are asking us to consider this suggestion. We have not yet really applied our mind to it.”
Strong growth in Q1
“The reports I am getting from industry seem to suggest that the first quarter has gone quite well. Export has been up 15%. So, my own sense is the first quarter will once again give very good results. Despite all the global uncertainties and challenges, we were the fastest-growing large economy last year, probably the first quarter will continue to show that India is a resilient nation, on the move,” he said.
Goyal said that while FTAs open doors to overseas markets, there is a large domestic economy that companies can tap. While trade with West Asia is normalising, Goyal said that efforts are underway to open new routes on the eastern sides, be it oil and gas pipelines or train lines.
Japan’s demand
The minister said that Japan has demanded restoration of benefit for a chemical that is used in the semiconductor value chain and govt will seek to ensure that the benefit, which was withdrawn due to misuse, is tapped properly.

briefs.bodyText:
OSAKA: Daikin Thursday said that it is lining up fresh investments of Rs 2,800 crore, of which around Rs 1,300 crore will go towards R&D for chillers and high capacity air conditioners that can also be used in data centres.
During his meeting, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal is learnt to have suggested to Daikin Industries president and COO Naofumi Takaneka that the Japanese company should go beyond assembling compressors to also manufacture them in India, including their components. Takaneka is learnt to have responded by saying that the R&D centre will seek to develop products that are conducive for Indian climate.
Takaneka told TOI that Daikin is keen to be present across the segments — from residential to commercial establishments as well as data centres. Since setting up the Neemrana factory in 2009, Daikin set up a JV for compressors in 2025 and has its own compressor unit as part of the PLI scheme for white goods. It’s R&D centre and innovation centre are due to be ready by 2028.

stories.headline: Groundsman who clashed with Gambhir placed on leave after fresh controversy
stories.deck: Groundsman Lee Fortis is on leave after an altercation with an ECB employee. This incident occurred at The Oval before a Hundred fixture. Fortis previously had a heated exchange with India coach Gautam Gambhir. He has been The Oval's head groundsman since 2012. His future role at the venue remains uncertain.
stories.bodyText:
Surrey groundsman Lee Fortis, who made headlines last year after a heated confrontation with India head coach 
Gautam Gambhir
 at The Oval, has been placed on leave following a separate altercation with an ECB employee.
Fortis was involved in a heated exchange with the employee while preparations were under way for a Hundred fixture. The ECB employee was reportedly left in tears following the incident.
The episode took place at The Oval on July 28, a day before MI London faced London Spirit at the venue, with both teams training at the ground.
Soon afterwards, Surrey chief executive Steve Elworthy was seen having a firm discussion with Fortis on the field. The groundsman subsequently left the playing area and has not returned to The Oval since.
It remains unclear whether Fortis will return, with some sources in the English game reportedly believing that he may not resume his role.
Fortis previously clashed with Gambhir
Fortis is a well-known figure around The Oval and attracted significant attention last year after an argument with Gambhir during India's Test against England.
The disagreement centred on the condition of the square, with Gambhir telling Fortis: “You’re just a groundsman, nothing beyond that.”
India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak subsequently described Fortis as “arrogant”.
Fortis has served as The Oval's head groundsman since 2012, taking up the role at the age of 30. He has since established himself as one of the leading groundsmen in English cricket, winning the ECB's Grounds Manager of the Year award three consecutive times from 2022 to 2024.
During that period, Surrey also won three successive County Championship titles.
The latest incident has now left one of English cricket's most recognisable groundsmen, who stands around 6ft 10in tall, away from The Oval while the circumstances surrounding his absence remain unclear.

stories.headline: ‘Got to learn from the opposition’: Gill reflects after SL deny IND clean sweep
stories.deck: India's captain, Shubman Gill, noted the need for growth following the drawn Test with Sri Lanka, recognizing key takeaways for the team. Devdutt Padikkal's stellar run with consistent centuries earned him the Player of the Series accolade, while Manav Suthar's wicket-taking skills received commendation. Sri Lanka's lower order showcased resilience to secure the draw. Now, India sets its sights…
stories.bodyText:
India captain 
Shubman Gill
 admitted there were plenty of lessons for his side despite the disappointment of missing out on a series clean sweep against Sri Lanka, while backing the team to respond strongly when they travel to New Zealand later this year.
India had to settle for a draw in the second Test at Colombo after Sri Lanka's lower order produced a determined fightback, led by Sonal Dinusha's unbeaten 133. India still won the two-match series 1-0, but the dropped opportunity to secure another victory affected their World Test Championship points percentage, leaving them fifth in the standings ahead of the New Zealand series beginning on November 19.
Speaking in a video by BCCI, Gill said the way Sri Lanka battled over the final three days deserved recognition and felt India could take lessons from their opponents as well.
"A lot of learnings in this series. I think we played decently well. Obviously not the result that we wanted in this match. After day two, we hoped that it was going to be a win for us, and then Sri Lanka batting the way that they did for these three days. Sometimes you have got to learn from the opposition as well and give credit to them for the way that they played, and hopefully we have a good series in New Zealand."
Gill praises Padikkal's impact
One of the biggest positives for India was the form of Devdutt Padikkal, who was named Player of the Series after producing two centuries.
With Sai Sudharsan unavailable because of injury, Padikkal made the most of his opportunity and strengthened his case for the No. 3 position in India's Test batting order.
Gill was particularly impressed by Padikkal's ability to convert good starts into substantial scores.
"We speak about once a batsman is set, he should make the most of it, and Devdutt showed that. Very positive signs for us, and the way he batted in the series was a treat to watch, you know, truly tells the mindset of a player, and that is a great positive sign for us," said Gill about Paddikal.
Padikkal ended the series as India's leading run-scorer, making 328 runs in three innings at an average of 109.33. His tally included two centuries and a highest score of 167.
Across his four Tests and six innings so far, Padikkal has accumulated 418 runs at an average of 69.66, with two centuries and one fifty.
Gill identifies Suthar as future spin leader
Gill also singled out Manav Suthar for praise after the left-arm spinner emerged as India's leading wicket-taker in the series.
Suthar's standout moment came in the first Test at Galle, where he claimed 10 wickets to register the first ten-wicket haul of his career. Gill believes the spinner has the qualities to become a long-term leader of India's spin attack.
"He has been magnificent for us, and I think he is going to be someone who is going to be leading the spin attack for India for a very long time. And the way he bowled in this match and even in the first match was a treat to watch. Every time he comes on to bowl, it feels like he is going to create those chances and going to get us wickets, and hopefully he keeps doing that," said the skipper.
Suthar finished the two-Test series with 16 wickets at an average of 21.06. His haul included a four-wicket spell and a six-wicket haul in the first Test, while his best innings figures were 6/55.
Dinusha leads Sri Lanka's fightback
India's first-innings total of 503/9 was built around three-figure knocks from Padikkal and Dhruv Jurel.
Padikkal made 117 from 193 balls, hitting 12 fours, while Jurel remained unbeaten on 115 from 177 deliveries, with nine fours and two sixes. Rishabh Pant contributed 63 from 89 balls, including six fours and two sixes, while Gill scored 50 from 108 balls with six fours.
Asitha Fernando was Sri Lanka's most successful bowler, finishing with four wickets.
Sri Lanka responded with 290 in their first innings. Dinusha again played a central role, scoring 103 from 162 balls with eight fours and three sixes. Pasindu Sooriyabandara added a valuable 80 from 133 balls, striking nine fours.
Prasidh Krishna and Suthar claimed three wickets apiece for India.
Asked to follow on, Sri Lanka were reduced to 218/6 before Dinusha and Keshara Nuwantha launched a stubborn recovery. The pair added 112 runs, with Nuwantha making 46 from 150 balls, including four boundaries.
Dinusha completed another century, remaining unbeaten on 133 from 264 deliveries with eight fours and two sixes. His resistance, combined with a lower-order effort that repeatedly frustrated India's bowlers, carried Sri Lanka to 429/9.
The draw ended India's hopes of a 2-0 series victory, but Gill believes the experience can prove valuable when India return to Test action in New Zealand in November.

stories.headline: 22 cricketers awarded annual contracts by Mumbai Cricket Association
stories.deck: The contracted players have been divided into three grades, with Grade A players receiving ₹12 lakh annually, Grade B ₹8 lakh and Grade C ₹6 lakh
stories.bodyText:
Twenty-two cricketers — 14 male and eight female — have been awarded annual contracts by the Mumbai Cricket Association. The MCA Apex Council has also constituted the Ajinkya Rahane Scholarship Fund, in a bid to recognise the distinguished career of the former India captain who retired from all formats earlier this month.
The decisions were taken at the Apex Council meeting on Thursday (August 27, 2026), with the player contract system being introduced to provide financial support to Mumbai cricketers who are not centrally contracted by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) or part of its list of targeted players.
The contracted players have been divided into three grades, with Grade A players receiving ₹12 lakh annually, Grade B ₹8 lakh and Grade C ₹6 lakh.
Siddhesh Lad and Shams Mulani are the two men in Grade A, while Mohit Avasthi, Aakash Anand and Hardik Tamore have been placed in Grade B.
Eight players, including Suved Parkar, Sairaj Patil and Himanshu Singh, form the Grade C list.
Among the women, Humairaa Kaazi and Vrushali Bhagat are the two Grade A players, while Sanika Chalke has been placed in Grade B. Five others, including Prakashika Naik and Fatima Jaffer are the Grade C players.
The MCA had announced earlier this year that it would initiate a player contract system for those outside the BCCI’s central contract and targeted-player structures. The move is aimed at providing greater recognition and financial security to players representing Mumbai.
The Apex Council also approved the Ajinkya Rahane Scholarship Fund in recognition of the former Mumbai captain’s journey from grassroots cricket to leading India in Test cricket. According to an MCA statement, the fund has received a contribution from former MCA president Sharad Pawar and will be used to support grassroots cricketers and the development of maidan cricket.
MCA president Ajinkya Naik said Rahane’s journey and achievements made him “an inspiration for young cricketers” and that the scholarship fund would help create greater opportunities at the grassroots. The Association also proposes to honour Rahane for his contribution to Mumbai and Indian cricket.

briefs.headline: Women’s Asia Cup 2026: Full schedule and squads; where to watch in India
briefs.deck: The eight teams have been divided into two groups. India, Pakistan, Thailand and Hong Kong are in Group A, while defending champions Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, the UAE and Indonesia make up Group B.
briefs.bodyText:
The 10th edition of the Women’s Asia Cup begins in Dubai on Friday, with eight teams competing in the T20I format. The tournament will run until September 13, with all 15 matches to be played in Dubai.
The eight teams have been divided into two groups. India, Pakistan, Thailand and Hong Kong are in Group A, while defending champions Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, the UAE and Indonesia make up Group B.
The top two teams from each group will qualify for the semi-finals. The two semi-finals will be played on September 10 and 11, followed by the final on September 13.
Sri Lanka will try to defend the title they won in 2024, while India will look to regain the trophy. Pakistan and Bangladesh are the other two Full Members in the tournament, while Thailand, Hong Kong, the UAE and Indonesia are the four Associate teams.
ALSO READ: Anything less than title will be a 'major disappointment' for  India in Women's Asia Cup
The tournament will feature one match every day during the group stage, which will continue until September 8. There will be 12 group-stage matches, followed by two semi-finals and the final.
Women's Asia Cup schedule
How did the Associate teams qualify?
Indonesia, Hong Kong, Thailand and the UAE earned their places in the Asia Cup through the 2026 Women's Premier Cup.
The Premier Cup featured 18 teams. All four qualified teams topped their respective groups and then won their quarter-finals to secure a place in the Asia Cup.
For Indonesia, this will be their first appearance in the Asia Cup. Hong Kong, meanwhile, will return to the tournament for the first time since 2012.
India-Pakistan clash on September 5
India and Pakistan will meet on September 5 in what is expected to be the main group-stage match.
India have won 14 of their 17 T20I meetings against Pakistan.
Sri Lanka will face Bangladesh on September 6 in another Group B match. Sri Lanka have won 13 of their 16 T20I meetings against Bangladesh.
India's Asia Cup record
India have won three of the five editions of the Women's Asia Cup played in the T20 format so far.
They finished runners-up in the other two editions, losing to Bangladesh in 2018 and Sri Lanka in 2024.
India will open their campaign against Thailand on August 30 before playing Hong Kong and Pakistan. Their match against Pakistan on September 5 is likely to be the main highlight of India's group campaign.
When will the matches start?
All Women’s Asia Cup 2026 matches will begin at 8pm IST.
Where to watch Women’s Asia Cup 2026?
In India, the tournament will be broadcast live on the Sony Sports Network television channels.
The matches will also be available for live streaming on the SonyLIV app and website.

briefs.headline: ‘Trying to kill him’: Imran Khan’s sons air explosive prison claims
briefs.deck: Imran Khan's sons have raised alarming issues regarding his health and living conditions in prison. They claim he is suffering from extended isolation and insufficient medical attention, with Kasim Khan revealing that their father's eyesight has notably deteriorated in one eye. Their attempts to visit him in Pakistan have been thwarted. Additionally, former international cricket captains are…
briefs.bodyText:
Sulaiman Khan and Kasim Khan, the sons of former Pakistan captain and Prime Minister Imran Khan, have expressed serious concern over their father’s health and the conditions in which he is being held in prison.
Speaking to former England captain and Sky Sports commentator Michael Atherton, the brothers alleged that Imran has been kept in prolonged isolation and has not received adequate medical care. They said they fear for his safety as he approaches three years in prison.
Kasim claimed that Imran has suffered a major loss of vision in one eye, estimating that he has lost around 80 per cent of his sight in it. He also said Imran was recently seen wearing an eye patch.
According to the brothers, Imran spends more than 23 hours a day alone inside a small cell, with restricted access to books and basic comforts. They also alleged that the cell does not have air conditioning despite the summer heat.
“They are not even acting with any kind of strategy any more. It is not very clear what they are doing, just blatantly trying to kill him in there. Keep him in as long as possible, and silence him. 
The last time he was able to speak to our aunties and anyone else, he said the conditions have severely worsened recently. He has been relating it to other political prisoners who have been killed or who have died in prison. Right now, it is worse than ever, completely isolating him more than 23 hours a day in a cell," Kasim said.
Sons fear for Imran’s health
Kasim said the priority for the family was now ensuring that Imran receives appropriate medical treatment. He described seeing his father with an eye patch and said the former Pakistan captain appeared visibly stressed.
“Right now, it’s really crucial for us that he gets proper treatment. He had an eye patch on for the eye situation, seemed visibly stressed, and that is something that is very hard for us to imagine because he embodies a very calm, assured presence, every time I have ever seen him, including being at gunpoint. A car we were in was robbed, and he was the calmest person there, including the robbers," he added.
The brothers also discussed their attempts to travel to Pakistan and visit their father. They claimed their visas had been blocked on technical grounds and said they were willing to accept the possibility of arrest if it gave them an opportunity to see Imran.
Sulaiman recalled the family's reaction after Imran was taken for a medical examination following a court order.
“We were cautiously optimistic. Our fears were confirmed when, instead of being taken to the private hospital, where he was meant to be taken, he was just taken to a government medical facility for a few hours, and then taken straight back to jail," said Sulaiman.
He claimed the examination at the government facility lasted only about an hour and that doctors waiting at Shifa Hospital were not given the opportunity to treat Imran.
“In reality, it was an hour check-up by government officials who said, ‘Great, he’s OK’, and then said we will now send him to the independent hospital, Shifa. Instead, they left all the doctors waiting, our auntie waiting, who is a doctor, and sent him straight back to jail," he added.
Interview sparks PCB controversy
The interview, which was aired during the lunch break of the second Test between England and Pakistan at Lord’s on Thursday, also created an unexpected controversy involving the PCB.
The board lodged a formal complaint with Sky Sports over the broadcast. Reports further suggested that the PCB considered asking Pakistan's players not to return to the field after lunch if the interview was shown.
The players eventually returned to the field and the Test continued as scheduled.
The interview came shortly after renewed international concern over Imran's medical treatment. He had been taken to a government hospital for a medical examination following a court order relating to his treatment.
Former captains back call for medical care
The concerns surrounding Imran have also drawn an appeal from a group of former international captains, including Indian cricket greats Sunil Gavaskar and Kapil Dev.
The former captains wrote to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, urging his government to ensure that Imran receives proper medical treatment and humane conditions while in prison.
The appeal was framed as a humanitarian intervention rather than a political statement.
Imran remains one of the most prominent figures in Pakistan cricket history. He led the country to its first men's ODI World Cup title in 1992 before entering politics and eventually becoming Pakistan's prime minister.

briefs.headline: Sonal Dinusha scripts history vs India, breaks Root's all-time 'sweeping' record
briefs.deck: The 25-year-old left-hander remained unbeaten on 133 in Sri Lanka's second innings as the hosts forced a draw in the second Test at the Sinhalese Sports Club in Colombo on Thursday. India still won the two-match series 1-0 after their victory in Galle.
briefs.bodyText:
Sonal Dinusha finished the two-Test series against India with another century and a new Test record, scoring 176 runs through sweep shots, the most by any batter in a Test series.
The 25-year-old left-hander remained unbeaten on 133 in Sri Lanka's second innings as the hosts forced a draw in the second Test at the Sinhalese Sports Club in Colombo on Thursday. India still won the two-match series 1-0 after their victory in Galle.
Dinusha's unbeaten 133 came after his first-innings 103 in Colombo and his century in the first Test in Galle. It was his third hundred in four innings in the series.
According to Cricinfo, Dinusha scored 176 runs through sweep shots across the series. The previous record was held by England's Joe Root, who scored 168 sweep-shot runs against Sri Lanka in 2021.
Dinusha also attempted 121 sweep shots during the series, another record for the most sweeps played by a batter in a Test series. Root had attempted 113 sweeps in the 2021 series.
After India enforced the follow-on with a first-innings lead of 213 runs, Sri Lanka batted for 243.4 overs across their two innings. Dinusha faced a total of 426 balls in the match.
He added 112 runs for the seventh wicket with Keshara Nuwantha, who scored 46, as the pair frustrated India's bowlers on the final day.
Sri Lanka resumed Day 5 at 229/6 and continued batting until both teams agreed to end the match with the score at 429/9. Sri Lanka finished with an overall lead of 216 runs.
For India, Manav Suthar returned figures of 3/121 in 41 overs, while Ravindra Jadeja took 3/94 in 38.3 overs.
Dinusha also became only the sixth batter in Test history to score three centuries in a series while batting at No. 6 or lower. He is the first Sri Lankan to achieve that feat and the first player to do it in a two-match Test series.
With his two centuries in Colombo, Dinusha also became only the fifth batter to score hundreds in both innings of a Test while batting at No. 6 or lower. Three of the previous four instances were also by Sri Lankan batters.

briefs.headline: PCB threatens player protest after Atherton’s interview with Imran Khan’s sons
briefs.deck: The Pakistan Cricket Board objected to Sky Sports airing an interview with Imran Khan's sons. The interview focused on their father's health and safety concerns while imprisoned. Sky Sports initially delayed the broadcast before showing it during the lunch interval. Khan's sons discussed their father's medical condition and access to treatment. This controversy arose after a Supreme Court order…
briefs.bodyText:
The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has reportedly raised an objection with Sky Sports after former England captain Michael Atherton interviewed the two sons of Imran Khan during the lunch break on the opening day of the Test at Lord’s.
According to Cricinfo, the PCB complained to the broadcaster over the decision to air the 18-minute interview with Suleiman Khan and Kasim Khan, which focused on their father’s health and concerns over his safety in prison.
The episode created an unusual off-field controversy around the Test, with the PCB reportedly even considering whether Pakistan’s players should remain off the field when play was due to resume for the second session.
PCB warned of possible player protest
Atherton conducted the interview with Suleiman and Kasim on Wednesday at Lord’s, a day before the Test began. Sky Sports had also used a preview of the conversation in its coverage ahead of the match.
According to Cricinfo, the PCB contacted Sky Sports before lunch on Thursday and objected to the planned broadcast. The board reportedly warned that Pakistan’s players could refuse to return to the field if the interview was aired.
Sky Sports initially held back the segment before eventually showing it during the lunch interval.
The interview was not broadcast in Pakistan because state broadcaster PTV holds the television rights for the series.
Imran’s sons speak about his health
During their conversation with Atherton, Suleiman and Kasim discussed their concerns about their father's condition and safety while he remains in prison.
The brothers also spoke about their efforts to ensure that Imran receives appropriate medical treatment.
The former Pakistan captain and 1992 World Cup-winning skipper has been incarcerated for around three years, with his health and access to medical care becoming an increasingly prominent concern for his family.
His sons have stepped up their public calls for greater access to medical treatment in recent weeks.
Supreme Court order adds to concerns
The latest controversy comes after Pakistan's Supreme Court last week directed that Imran be admitted to Shifa Hospital in Islamabad.
However, instead of being taken to the hospital named in the directive, Imran was taken to the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) for a medical check-up before being returned to prison.
His sisters and sons have alleged that the authorities did not follow the court's directive. They have also continued to demand that Imran be examined by his own doctor.
The developments have prompted former international cricketers to publicly call for better medical care for the former Pakistan captain.
Atherton among former captains backing Imran
Last week, 21 former international captains, including Atherton, signed a letter to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif urging authorities to ensure that Imran receives proper medical attention while in custody.
The signatories included former captains from India, Australia, England, New Zealand and the West Indies.
It followed another appeal in February, when 14 former international captains wrote to the Pakistan government on the issue. Reports said that letter did not receive a response.
The PCB has not publicly commented on the reported complaint against Sky Sports.
The Pakistan government has previously rejected allegations that Imran has been mistreated in prison or denied access to his family and legal representatives.
Speaking to the Associated Press last week, the government said Imran had received more than 900 visits from relatives, lawyers and doctors since his imprisonment in August 2023.

briefs.headline: Asia Cup: Anything less than title will be a 'disappointment' for India
briefs.deck: Given the historic dominance of the Indian team in the tournament, former India cricketer and ex-women's team coach WV Raman believes anything less than a title in the upcoming 2026 Women's Asia Cup would be a "major disappointment" for Harmanpreet Kaur's team.
briefs.bodyText:
India have won seven of the nine Women's Asia Cup editions played so far, across ODI and T20I formats, making them the most successful team in the history of the tournament.
Given the historic dominance of the Indian team in the tournament, former India cricketer and ex-women's team coach WV Raman believes anything less than a title in the upcoming 2026 Women's Asia Cup would be a "major disappointment" for 
Harmanpreet Kaur
's team.
"Pakistan and Sri Lanka will be tough competition for India, and let's not also discount Thailand, because they've shown a lot of enthusiasm, they've shown they've got some real good talent there, and you cannot take them lightly, too. As far as the Indian team is concerned, I think anything less than a victory will be seen as a major disappointment," Raman said in an exclusive interview with TimesofIndia.com, organised by Sony Sports Network.
India lost the 2024 Women's Asia Cup final to Chamari Athapaththu's Sri Lanka by eight wickets in Dambulla, and Raman said "India can regain the Asia Cup" in Dubai.
However, the road ahead is not as smooth for India as it seems. India have been missing two of their pace-bowling all-rounders, Amanjot Kaur and Kashvee Gautam, for over five months, and just before the Asia Cup they faced another setback as Jemimah Rodrigues was also ruled out of the tournament due to a hamstring injury.
Pratika Rawal is in the side, but where should she bat?
Pratika Rawal has received her maiden India T20I call-up as Jemimah was ruled out of the tournament, and is expected to walk straight into the playing XI when India face Thailand on Sunday. However, the bigger question is where the right-handed batter fits into India's batting order.
"Pratika Rawal has done extremely well in Test cricket. She's done well in ODIs, but in T20s, we haven't seen much of her so far. And also the other thing that they need to work out is her slot in the batting order. So where does she bat is something they've got to try and work out," former women's team coach Raman said.
Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana will most likely not be separated as an opening pair, and Bharti Fulmali and Richa Ghosh could play the role of lower-order enforcers. Captain Harmanpreet Kaur bats at four when Jemimah plays at three in T20Is; however, Raman argued that Kaur should instead bat at three in the Asia Cup.
"I doubt if they will have Pratika Rawal at number three. I would rather imagine that Harmanpreet Kaur herself might bat at number three because she needs to spend a lot of time there at the crease, have more overs at her disposal to try and pace the innings," WV Raman said in an interview with TimesofIndia.com, adding, "Will India play Pratika at number four is something that will be a big question. As I see it, they need to obviously find ways and methods to use the 20 overs allotted to them in the most productive manner possible. So it's up to them to try and see."
Longer rope for Fulmali
Fulmali ended her seven-year exile from international cricket earlier this year when she was picked for the South Africa tour and was also retained for the T20 World Cup.
Among all the batters who have faced at least 100 balls in the Women's Premier League (WPL) since 2024, India's Richa Ghosh (155.05) and Bharti Fulmali (149.76) are at number two and three in terms of the strike rate, respectively.
However, India dropped Fulmali from the team after just one innings in the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup where there campaign ended in the group stage.
The former India cricketer said that the Women's Asia Cup is the ideal tournament to give Fulmali consistent chances.
"If they have plans for Fulmali in the near future or for the next couple of years, to be an integral part of the batting unit, then probably this is as good an opportunity as they'll get to try and give her a lot of chances and see how she fares," WV Raman said.
"Fulmali has the reputation of being a big hitter. She was picked up in the side about six years ago. Then again, she was out in the wilderness. Then again, she's come back, and then she's gone out, and she's come back. I think this is something that needs to be looked at very seriously because you're not doing anybody a favour by just giving them one odd chance here and there sporadically," he added.
The former coach of the women's team also emphasized that India should look at the Asia Cup as a tournament where they begin preparation for the 2028 Women's T20 World Cup after their unceremonious group-stage exit in the 2026 T20 World Cup.
"They (India) can look at this Asia Cup as a platform from which they'll start planning for the next T20 World Cup in terms of planning, in terms of working out different combinations, looking at various options. So that will be a good thing to do starting from this Asia Cup, and even though you can't equate a terrific performance in the T20 World cup to a victory in Asia cup, if they go on to win this Asia cup, as we are expecting them to, it'll provide them some solace after probably the unexpected early exit in the T20 World Cup," WV Raman noted.

briefs.headline: Smith and Cox revive England against Pakistan after Abbas strikes
briefs.deck: Veteran paceman Mohammad Abbas took three wickets for four runs in 16 balls, including the prize scalp of England captain Joe Root for four, as the hosts slumped to 36-3, after Pakistan won the toss in helpful conditions for seam bowling
briefs.bodyText:
Jamie Smith and Jordan Cox both scored fifties as England recovered from a top-order collapse against Pakistan to reach 248-9 when bad light ended Thursday's (August 27, 2026) opening day of the second Test at Lord's.
Veteran paceman Mohammad Abbas took three wickets for four runs in 16 balls, including the prize scalp of England captain Joe Root for four, as the hosts slumped to 36-3, after Pakistan won the toss in helpful conditions for seam bowling.
But Smith's 61 and 55 from number three Cox — his second fifty in successive Test innings — got England back into the game.
Abbas had fine figures of 4-56 in 15 overs and fellow seamer Mohammad Ali 3-67 in 17 when the umpires ruled it was unsafe to continue despite the floodlights illuminating the ground.
"I think it is a decent enough day for us," Smith told Sky Sports after the close. "The ball was doing enough, nipping around — overhead conditions obviously assisted.
"Pakistan bowled nicely and showed that when you take wickets with the new ball you can start to put teams under a bit more pressure."
Pakistan were woeful in all departments during an innings and 103-run defeat in the first of a three-Test series at Headingley last week.
They did, however, have the worst of the conditions after losing the toss before being dismissed for meagre totals of 171 and 135.
Fine catch
It was a different story in London, with Pakistan captain Babar Azam opting to field on a green-tinged pitch under grey skies following a rain delay.
Azam was the only change to either side, as he returned from a finger injury in place of stand-in skipper Salman Ali Agha.
England had dropped fast bowler Brydon Carse, who did not play in the first Test, from their squad after another late-night drinking incident.
Abbas, who has had stints with several English counties, was soon into his stride on a ground where he was named player of the match after taking eight wickets in Pakistan's victory in their last Test at Lord's in 2018.
The 36-year-old was fortunate, however, when Emilio Gay glanced a legside ball only for diving wicket-keeper Mohammad Rizwan to hold an excellent one-handed catch.
Ben Duckett fell for 17 when lbw to an Abbas nip-backer.
Medium-pace bowling with the 'keeper standing up to the stumps has plagued England in recent times and Rizwan was up to the wicket when Abbas pinned Root on the back leg.
Harry Brook was then bowled for 15 by a superb Ali delivery that jagged back, with England 80-4 at lunch.
Dan Lawrence had made 10 when he flicked to midwicket only for Shan Masood to drop a seemingly routine catch.
Pakistan's fielding was poor as they tumbled to the bottom of the World Test Championship table with defeat in Leeds.
But when Lawrence turned spinner Ali Usman legside and set off for a non-existent single, only to be sent back by Cox, he was run out by Masood's accurate throw from mid-wicket to Rizwan.
Cox struck consecutive legside boundaries off Usman to complete an 88-ball fifty including seven fours.
His partnership of 67 with Smith ended when substitute fielder Agha held a superb catch at second slip off Khurram Shahzad.
Smith, whose fifty came from a mere 63 balls, was clean bowled by Ali and two balls later the paceman dismissed tailender Ollie Robinson with another nip-backer.
Jofra Archer straight-drove Abbas for six before the bowler had his revenge, with Gus Atkinson — who has a Test century at Lord's to his credit — a useful 34 not out at stumps.

briefs.headline: Women’s T20 Asia Cup: Harmanpreet Kaur says India not focusing on any particular team
briefs.deck: The Asia Cup features India, Pakistan, defending champions Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, hosts UAE, Thailand, Hong Kong China, and Indonesia
briefs.bodyText:
India captain Harmanpreet Kaur on Thursday (August 27, 2026) said her team is not singling out any opponent in the Women's T20 Asia Cup and will instead focus on playing good cricket, while expecting a challenging tournament with the standard of Asian teams improving rapidly.
The Asia Cup features India, Pakistan, defending champions Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, hosts UAE, Thailand, Hong Kong China, and Indonesia.
The ODI world champions India enter the Women's T20 Asia Cup as one of the favourites, but Harmanpreet played down the hype surrounding her team's much-anticipated clash against Pakistan on September 5. The Indian skipper said her team would not allow external factors to distract it.
"We are not putting any focus on one particular team, which is going to be tough for us. All the teams have been doing well and our focus is to play good cricket and not to take any team easily," Harmanpreet said at the captains' press conference ahead of the tournament, which begins in Dubai on Friday (August 28, 2026).
"Our main focus is just playing cricket, other than giving focus to the other impact of the game." Harmanpreet did not answer if she would shake hands with her Pakistani counterpart Fatima Sana.
The India skipper said they are treating the continental tournament as an opportunity to test themselves under pressure and build on the lessons from their recent experiences.
"Asia Cup is a platform where you can really test yourself and put yourself under a lot of pressure to perform at a level which you expect a lot from your team," Harmanpreet said.
"This tournament is very important for us as a team to do well. Especially all the teams, they are the ones in the last two-three years we have seen massive improvement. And whenever we are playing against them, they are not giving anything easy to us.
"This is going to be very challenging, but at the same time, our experience will help us." India had a disappointing T20 World Cup campaign, but Harmanpreet believes the experiences gained from past matches will stand the team in good stead.
"All the experience we have got from the past matches is going to help us, and hopefully we will play our best cricket and enjoy cricket here," she said.
Asked about India's preparation for the hot and humid Dubai conditions, Harmanpreet said the team would use its training sessions and the matches preceding their opener to assess the conditions before finalising their combination.
"We just reached yesterday (Wednesday) and haven't seen the field yet. But tomorrow (Friday) when we train, even a good thing is that two teams are playing before us. So we will get to see a lot of things and then understand how the conditions are going to be. And then accordingly, we'll make the plan," she said.
Harmanpreet said packed stands, such as those witnessed during India's women's clash against Pakistan in Dubai in 2024, were a welcome sign for the sport.
"As a cricketer, we always want to see packed stadiums. Fans are coming and supporting us. Hopefully, this Asia Cup, we have the same packed stadiums," she said.
Harmanpreet also backed the Indian squad amid questions raised over selection by former captain Anjum Chopra.
"I don't know what you're talking about, but I think we have picked the best team and they have given very impressive performances. That's why they are here. I'm sure that whenever we go to the field, we'll play our best cricket," she said.

briefs.headline: Divya Deshmukh to make Global Chess League debut with defending champions Alpine Pipers
briefs.deck: Divya Deshmukh’s teammates include the World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen and fellow Indian Arjun Erigaisi
briefs.bodyText:
Divya Deshmukh, the women’s World Cup winner, is looking forward to her maiden Global Chess League. She will play for Alpine Pipers in the fourth edition of the GCL, beginning in Bengaluru on September 5.
Her teammates include the World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen and fellow Indian Arjun Erigaisi.
“It’s my debut, so I’m definitely very excited,” Divya said.
“It’s not like any other chess tournament. There’s going to be a lot of audience for this one, which is really nice. Playing in India is always fun.”
Divya is also keen to explore GCL’s format. “I can’t say anything about the format now. This is going to be my first event in Bengaluru. I have only been to the Bengaluru airport before.”
The GCL, a joint venture between Tech Mahindra and the global chess governing body FIDE, will be held at Lalit Ashok and conclude on September 13.
